        let mut membership=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT octet_length(child_id),child_id FROM temp._extraction_each_children WHERE parent_id=?1 ORDER BY child_id")?;
        let mut members = membership.query([id])?;
        while let Some(member) = members.next()? {
            meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
            let id_bytes:i64=member.get(0)?;
            meter.heap((id_bytes.max(0) as u64).saturating_mul(8).saturating_add(512))?;
            let child_id: String = member.get(1)?;
            let image = read_image(tx, ct, &child_id, meter, false)?.ok_or_else(|| {
                refuse("extract each child disappeared from its activation snapshot")
            })?;
            let child_id = child_id.as_str();
            if !anchored(tx, ct, child_id, key, pt, id)? {
                return Err(refuse(
                    "extract each child lacks valid parent-lifetime evidence; refusing deletion/id reuse or retrospective recapture",
                ));
            }
            if let Some(through) = &child.through {
                let parent_image = crate::schema::row_image(&row, current_parent);
                if through.fields.iter().any(|(capture, field)| {
                    image.field(capture).ok() != parent_image.field(field).ok()
                }) {
                    return Err(refuse(
                        "reverse extract each would change captured parent authority; preserve the child audience in an authored bridge",
                    ));
                }
            }
            let asset_value=image.field(destination)?;
            meter.heap(asset_value.retained_heap_bytes().saturating_mul(4).saturating_add(512))?;
            let v = asset_value.clone();
            let asset_id = asset_id(&v)?;
            let position:Option<i64>=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT position FROM _extraction_each_rows WHERE definition=?1 AND child_t=?2 AND child_id=?3",params![key,ct,child_id],|r|r.get(0)).optional()?;
            children.push((
                position.unwrap_or(i64::MAX),
                child_id.to_owned(),
                image,
                v,
                asset_id,
            ));
        }
        drop(members);
        drop(membership);
        children.sort_by(|a, b| (&a.0, &a.1).cmp(&(&b.0, &b.1)));
        let mut values = Vec::new();
        let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
        for (position, (_, child_id, mut image, v, asset_id)) in children.into_iter().enumerate() {
            meter.charge(MeterKind::RowsWritten, 1)?;
            if !seen.insert(asset_id.clone()) {
                return Err(refuse(
                    "extract each found competing child homes for one asset",
                ));
            }
            for (dest, src) in &e.fields {
                if dest != destination && row.field(src).ok() != image.field(dest).ok() {
                    return Err(refuse(
                        "extract each immutable scalar copies disagree with the current parent",
                    ));
                }
            }
            transfer(
                tx,
                &v,
                (&e.child, &child_id, destination),
                (&e.parent, id, source),
            )?;
            fields(&mut image)?.remove(destination);
            write(tx, ct, &child_id, &image)?;
            tx.conn().execute(
                "DELETE FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND column_name=?3",
                params![ct, child_id, destination],
            )?;
            save(tx, key, pt, id, ct, &child_id, &asset_id, position)?;
            values.push(v);
            count += 1;
        }
        let was_null:bool=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _extraction_cells WHERE definition=?1 AND parent_t=?2 AND parent_id=?3 AND column_name=?4 AND data=?5)",params![key,pt,id,source,canonical_json(&Value::Null)],|r|r.get(0))?;
        let list = if values.is_empty()
            && kind.is_optional()
            && was_null
        {
            Value::Null
        } else {
            Value::Array(values)
        };
        remember(tx, key, pt, id, source, &list, meter)?;
        fields(&mut row)?.insert(source.into(), list);
        write(tx, pt, id, &row)?;
        Ok(())
    })?;
    tx.conn()
        .execute_batch("DROP TABLE temp._extraction_each_children;")?;
    report.backfills.push(format!(
        "extract {} each: moved {count} child asset homes back into parent lists",
        e.child
    ));
    Ok(())
}

//! Typed one-child extraction; home transfer is an activation operation.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#20-visible-rollback-views-roll — an asset is moved with its one home.
use super::*;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Extraction {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")]
    pub each: bool,
    pub child: String,
    pub parent: String,
    pub reference: String,
    pub fields: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}
impl Extraction {
    pub fn admit(&self, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), String> {
        if schema.extractions.iter().filter(|e|e.child==self.child).count()>1 {
            return Err("one extraction declaration owns each child table; native children cannot be assigned to competing sources".into());
        }
        let child = schema
            .table(&self.child)
            .ok_or("extraction child is not declared")?;
        if self.child == self.parent
            || schema.table(&self.parent).is_none()
            || child.ephemeral.is_some()
            || schema.maintain_for(&self.child).is_some()
        {
            return Err("extraction needs distinct authoritative durable parent and child tables without captured ownership".into());
        }
        if child.columns.get(&self.reference)
            != Some(&ColumnType::Ref {
                table: self.parent.clone(),
            })
        {
            return Err("extraction needs a required reference to its parent".into());
        }
        if !matches!(
            child.on_delete.get(&self.reference),
            Some(references::OnDelete::Cascade | references::OnDelete::Restrict)
        ) {
            return Err("reversible extraction requires on delete cascade or restrict; kept references cannot prove the parent lifetime".into());
        }
        if self.fields.is_empty()
            || self.fields.contains_key(&self.reference)
            || self.fields.keys().any(|c| {
                !child.columns.contains_key(c)
                    || c == "id"
                    || child.engine_field(c)
                    || child.maintained.contains_key(c)
                    || child.sequences.contains_key(c)
                    || child.written_by.contains_key(c)
            })
        {
            return Err("extraction fields must be distinct authoritative child columns".into());
        }
        if self.each {
            let assets:Vec<_>=self.fields.keys().filter(|c|asset(&child.columns[*c])).collect();
            if assets.len()!=1 || !matches!(child.columns[assets[0]],ColumnType::Image{..}|ColumnType::File{..}|ColumnType::Video{..}) {
                return Err("extract each requires exactly one required scalar image/file/video destination; map its historical bounded list".into());
            }
        }
        if !self.fields.keys().any(|c| asset(&child.columns[c])) {
            return Err("extraction needs at least one mapped image/file column".into());
        }
        if child.columns.iter().any(|(c, k)| {
            c != &self.reference
                && c != "id"
                && !self.fields.contains_key(c)
                && !k.is_optional()
                && !child.defaults.contains_key(c)
                && !child.engine_field(c)
        }) {
            return Err("map every required child column or give it an explicit default".into());
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
pub(super) fn asset(k: &ColumnType) -> bool {
    match k {
        ColumnType::Optional(k)
        | ColumnType::List { of: k, .. }
        | ColumnType::ListRange { of: k, .. } => asset(k),
        ColumnType::Image { .. } | ColumnType::File { .. } | ColumnType::Video { .. } => true,
        _ => false,
    }
}

//! One-child historical extraction moves the existing asset home atomically.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#20-visible-rollback-views-roll — deterministic identities, no upload or second home.
use super::*;
#[path = "extraction_each.rs"]
mod each;

    meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter},
    schema::{ColumnType, Extraction},
};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
fn refuse(s: impl Into<String>) -> RuntimeError {
    RuntimeError::Structural {
        code: "E_ADOPT",
        message: s.into(),
    }
}
fn asset(k: &ColumnType) -> bool {
    match k {
        ColumnType::Optional(k)
        | ColumnType::List { of: k, .. }
        | ColumnType::ListRange { of: k, .. } => asset(k),
        ColumnType::Image { .. } | ColumnType::File { .. } | ColumnType::Video { .. } => true,
        _ => false,
    }
}
fn fields(row: &mut Value) -> Result<&mut crate::value::ObjectFields, RuntimeError> {
    match row {
        Value::Row(f) | Value::Map(f) => Ok(f),
        _ => Err(refuse("invalid extraction row")),
    }

fn key(tx:&Tx<'_>,e:&Extraction)->Result<String,RuntimeError>{
    let parent=tx.num(&e.parent)?;let child=tx.num(&e.child)?;
    let aliases:bool=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name='_asset_column_renames')",[],|r|r.get(0))?;
    let origin=|t:i64,c:&str|->Result<String,RuntimeError>{
        if !aliases{return Ok(c.into())}
        Ok(tx.conn().query_row("SELECT origin FROM _asset_column_renames WHERE t=?1 AND name=?2",params![t,c],|r|r.get(0)).optional()?.unwrap_or_else(||c.into()))
    };
    let fields=e.fields.iter().map(|(dest,source)|Ok((origin(child,dest)?,origin(parent,source)?))).collect::<Result<BTreeMap<_,_>,RuntimeError>>()?;
    let base=(parent,child,origin(child,&e.reference)?,fields);
    Ok(if e.each {crate::value::digest(&("each-v1",base))}else{crate::value::digest(&base)})
}

fn load(tx: &Tx<'_>, t: i64, id: &str) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
    let bytes: Option<i64> = tx
        .conn()
        .query_row(
            "SELECT octet_length(data) FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",
            params![t, id],
            |r| r.get(0),
        )
        .optional()?;
    let Some(bytes) = bytes else { return Ok(None) };
    Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort).heap(
        (bytes.max(0) as u64)
            .saturating_mul(64)
            .saturating_add(8192),
    )?;
    let text: String = tx.conn().query_row(
        "SELECT data FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2",
        params![t, id],
        |r| r.get(0),
    )?;
    serde_json::from_str(&text)
        .map(Some)
        .map_err(|e| refuse(e.to_string()))
}
fn write(tx: &Tx<'_>, t: i64, id: &str, row: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    tx.conn().execute("INSERT INTO r(t,id,data) VALUES(?1,?2,?3) ON CONFLICT(t,id) DO UPDATE SET data=excluded.data",params![t,id,canonical_json(row)])?;
    Ok(())
}
fn value(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    t: i64,
    id: &str,
    row: &Value,
    c: &str,
) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
    if let Ok(v) = row.field(c) {
        return Ok(Some(v.clone()));
    }
    let text: Option<String> = tx
        .conn()
        .query_row(
            "SELECT data FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND column_name=?3",

        )
        .optional()?;
    text.map(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).map_err(|e| refuse(e.to_string())))
        .transpose()
}
fn transfer(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    v: &Value,
    from: (&str, &str, &str),
    to: (&str, &str, &str),
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if let Value::Array(vs) = v {
        for v in vs {
            transfer(tx, v, from, to)?;
        }
        return Ok(());
    }
    if v == &Value::Null {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let id = crate::assets::asset_id(Some(v))
        .ok_or_else(|| refuse("extraction asset has no typed ledger id"))?;
    let bytes:Option<i64>=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT bytes FROM _assets WHERE id=?1 AND home_table=?2 AND home_id=?3 AND home_column=?4 AND released_at IS NULL",params![id,from.0,from.1,from.2],|r|r.get(0)).optional()?;
    let bytes = bytes.ok_or_else(|| {
        refuse(format!(
            "extraction asset {id} has no live source home; never claim or duplicate it"
        ))
    })?;
    let root = tx
        .meta("activation_asset_root")?
        .ok_or_else(|| refuse("extraction requires activation asset custody"))?;
    if id.is_empty()
        || !id
            .bytes()
            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'-' || b == b'_')
    {
        return Err(refuse("invalid extraction asset id"));
    }
    let path = std::path::Path::new(&root).join(id);
    let meta = std::fs::symlink_metadata(&path)
        .map_err(|_| refuse(format!("extraction asset {id} bytes are unavailable")))?;
    if !meta.is_file() || meta.len() != bytes as u64 {
        return Err(refuse(format!(
            "extraction asset {id} byte length disagrees with its ledger"
        )));
    }
    if from != to {
    tx.conn().execute(
        "UPDATE _assets SET home_table=?2,home_id=?3,home_column=?4 WHERE id=?1",
        params![id, to.0, to.1, to.2],
    )?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
pub(super) fn transition(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    next: &Schema,
    previous: Option<&Schema>,
    sources: &BTreeMap<String, Table>,
    report: &mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

            write(tx, ct, &child_id, &image)?;

pub(super) fn delete(tx: &Tx<'_>, t: i64, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if exists(tx)? {
        each::delete(tx,t,id)?;
        tx.conn().execute(
            "DELETE FROM _extraction_cells WHERE parent_t=?1 AND parent_id=?2",
            params![t, id],
        )?;
        tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _extraction_rows WHERE (parent_t=?1 AND parent_id=?2) OR (child_t=?1 AND child_id=?2)",params![t,id])?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn observe_write(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    t: i64,
    id: &str,
    row: &Value,
    old: Option<&Value>,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if !exists(tx)? {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let active:Vec<(String,String,String)>=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT definition,parent_name,reference_column FROM _extraction_active WHERE child_t=?1")?.query_map([t],|r|Ok((r.get(0)?,r.get(1)?,r.get(2)?)))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
    for (key, parent, column) in active {
        let binding = format!("$extract:{key}");
        let existing: bool = tx.conn().query_row(
            "SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_refs WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND column_name=?3)",
            params![t, id, binding],
            |r| r.get(0),
        )?;
        if existing && old.is_some_and(|old| old.field(&column).ok() == row.field(&column).ok()) {
            continue;
        }
        if let Ok(value) = row.field(&column) {
            super::dormant::capture_refs(
                tx,
                t,
                id,
                &binding,
                &ColumnType::Ref { table: parent },
                value,
            )?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn retain_cell(
    tx: &Tx<'_>,
    key: &str,
    t: i64,
    id: &str,
    column: &str,
    value: &Value,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let old: Option<String> = tx
        .conn()
        .query_row(
            "SELECT data FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND column_name=?3",
            params![t, id, column],
            |r| r.get(0),
        )
        .optional()?;
    if let Some(old) = old {
        let old: Value = serde_json::from_str(&old).map_err(|e| refuse(e.to_string()))?;
        if &old != value {
            return Err(refuse(
                "extraction has a distinct retained source cell; preserve both meanings in an authored bridge",
            ));
        }
    }
    tx.conn().execute("INSERT INTO _extraction_cells VALUES(?1,?2,?3,?4,?5) ON CONFLICT(definition,parent_t,parent_id,column_name) DO UPDATE SET data=excluded.data",params![key,t,id,column,canonical_json(value)])?;
    Ok(())
}

//! Owner-mediated release publication in the running HTTP process.
use super::*;
use crate::release_control::Command;
#[cfg(unix)]
use crate::release_control::Listener;
use snapback4_core::engine::release::ReleaseActivation;

#[cfg(unix)]
pub(super) fn start(
    shared: Arc<Shared>,
    dir: std::path::PathBuf,
) -> Result<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>, String> {
    let store = shared
        .owner
        .as_ref()
        .ok_or("release control requires a persisted owner")?
        .path()
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let listener = Listener::bind(&dir, store)?;
    crate::lifecycle::managed_cleanup();
    crate::lifecycle::background("release-control", move || {
        listener.run(|command| apply(&shared, &dir, command))
    })
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#5-hot-activation-and-ownership — only assignments and committed rebind follow the database commit.
pub(super) fn apply(
    shared: &Shared,
    dir: &std::path::Path,
    command: Command,
) -> Result<Json, String> {
    match command {
        Command::Stop => {
            crate::lifecycle::request_stop();
            Ok(json!({"stopping":true}))
        }
        Command::Status {
            after,
            items_after,
            event,
        } => {
            shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
            let mut status=engine.store_mut().release_status(after,items_after.as_deref(),event).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            status["clock"]=json!({"now":shared.now(),"offsetMs":lock(&shared.clock).offset()});
            Ok(status)
            })
        },
        Command::Prune {
            confirm,
            expected_revision,
        } => {
            let mut result = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, _| engine.store_mut().prune_dormant(confirm, Some(expected_revision)))
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if let Some(items) = result["items"].as_array_mut() {
                items.truncate(16);
            }
            result["items_after"] = result["items"]
                .as_array()
                .and_then(|items| items.last())
                .map(|i| i["key"].clone())
                .unwrap_or(Json::Null);
            Ok(result)
        }
        Command::Activate {
            activation_protocol,
            release,
            expected_release,
            expected_revision,
            digest,
            rollback,
            visible_rollback,
            registry_custody,
            restore_dormant,
            allow_feed_adoption,
        } => {
            if activation_protocol != crate::release_control::ACTIVATION_PROTOCOL {
                return Err("release activation protocol differs; restart serve with this CLI before switching releases".into());
            }
            if release == 0 {
                return Err("release id must be positive".into());
            }
            let project = Project {
                root: dir.join("releases").join(release.to_string()),
            };
            if !std::fs::symlink_metadata(&project.root)
                .is_ok_and(|m| m.is_dir() && !m.file_type().is_symlink())
            {
                return Err(format!(
                    "release {release} is not an immutable release directory"
                ));
            }
            if !registry_custody{return Err("release custody requires an updated release-control client; use this runtime's CLI".into())}
            crate::verbs::validate_registered_view(dir,&project.root)?;
            if crate::release_files::digest(&project.root)? != digest {
                return Err("staged release content changed; redeploy its exact source".into());
            }
            if project.sources().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.is_empty() {
                return Err(format!(
                    "release {release} has no Quarry source; select a complete immutable release"
                ));
            }
            let bound = project.compile().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if !bound.diagnostics.is_empty() {
                return Err(bound
                    .diagnostics
                    .iter()
                    .map(ToString::to_string)
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                    .join("\n"));
            }
            let prepared = crate::native::prepare(&project, &bound).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            crate::dev_worker::prepare_release(&project, &bound.schema)?;
            crate::release_files::link_store(&project.root)?;
            if crate::release_files::digest(&project.root)? != digest {
                return Err("release artifacts changed during preparation; retry after inspecting immutable source".into());
            }
            crate::release_files::durable(&project.root)?;
            let mut pointer =
                crate::release_files::Pointer::prepare(dir, release, expected_release, rollback)?;
            let options = ReleaseActivation {
                visibility:crate::verbs::visibility_policy(&project.root)?.or_else(||visible_rollback.then(Default::default)),
                release,
                expected_previous: expected_release,
                expected_revision: Some(expected_revision),
                restore_dormant,
                native_digest: prepared.installed.as_ref().map(|m| m.digest.clone()),
                operation: if rollback { "rollback" } else { "deploy" }.into(),
            };
            let _requests=shared.release_requests.write();
            shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
            lock(&shared.readers).begin_adoption(&bound);
            let generation = match engine.adopt_release_at(
                bound.schema.clone(),
                bound.programs.iter().map(|p| p.program.clone()),
                &options,
                allow_feed_adoption,
                shared.now(),
            ) {
                Ok(generation) => generation,
                Err(error) => {
                    lock(&shared.readers).finish_adoption();
                    return Err(error.to_string());
                }
            };
            #[cfg(test)]
            test_work(&shared.release_committed);
            engine.set_prepared_native(prepared.module);
            engine.set_presence(Some(shared.presence.clone()));
            shared.refresh_time_audience_clock(engine, shared.now());
            lock(&shared.readers).replace(engine, &bound.refusal_sites);
            {
                let mut active = lock(&shared.bound);
                let mut advertised = lock(&shared.generation);
                let mut native = lock(&shared.native);
                shared.latency.adopt(&bound);
                *active = bound;
                *advertised = generation;
                *native = prepared.installed;
                let mut root = lock(&shared.release_root);
                *root = Some(project.root);
                shared.worker_revision.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Release);
            }
            crate::lifecycle::generation(generation);
            shared.publish_engine(engine);
            // Completion I/O can fail, but never abandons the new runtime.
            pointer.finish(generation)?;
            snapback4_core::diagnostic!(
                "snapback4 serve: release {release} activated without restart as generation {generation}"
            );
            Ok(
                json!({"release":release,"generation":generation,"revision":expected_revision+1,"hot":true,"adoption":engine.store().adoption_report().compact(),"details":engine.store().adoption_report().summary(),"backfills":engine.store().adoption_report().backfills}),
            )
            })
        }
    }
}

const groupClosures = new WeakMap<ChildProcess, Promise<void>>();
process.once("exit", () => { for (const child of children) child.kill("SIGKILL"); });
export function register(child: ChildProcess): void {
  children.add(child);
  child.once("exit", () => children.delete(child));

export function deadline(ms: number | undefined, fallback: number): number {
  const value = ms ?? fallback;
  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 1) throw new RangeError("proof timeout must be positive and finite");
  return value;
}
/** @throws deadline expires; work rejection propagates. */
export async function bounded<T>(work: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  try {
    return await Promise.race([work, new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
      timer = setTimeout(() => reject(Error(`${label} timed out after ${ms} ms`)), ms);
    })]);
  } finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
}
/** Attempts every cleanup, even if a preceding step fails or stalls. */
/** @throws AggregateError after every cleanup was attempted; each step has a 10-second bound. */
export async function cleanup(...steps: Array<(() => unknown | Promise<unknown>) | undefined>): Promise<void> {
  const errors: unknown[] = [];
  for (const step of steps) if (step) {
    try { await bounded(Promise.resolve().then(step), 10_000, "proof cleanup"); }
    catch (error) { errors.push(error); }
  }
  if (errors.length) throw new AggregateError(errors, "proof cleanup failed");
}
/** @throws invalid handle/deadline, host stop failure or TERM/KILL reap deadline. */
export async function stopChild(child: ChildProcess | Pick<ProofHost, "url" | "stop">, graceMs = 5000): Promise<void> {
  deadline(graceMs, 5000);
  if (child && "url" in child && typeof child.url === "string" && typeof child.stop === "function") {
    await bounded(Promise.resolve().then(() => child.stop()), graceMs + 10_000, "host stop"); return;
  }
  if (!child || !("kill" in child) || typeof child.kill !== "function" || typeof child.once !== "function"
      || !(child.exitCode === null || typeof child.exitCode === "number")
      || !(child.signalCode === null || typeof child.signalCode === "string")) {
    throw new TypeError("stopChild needs a ChildProcess or { url, stop }");
  }
  if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) { await groupGone(child); return; }
  let done!: () => void;
  const exited = new Promise<void>(resolve => { done = resolve; });
  child.once("exit", done);
  child.once("error", done);
  try {
    child.kill("SIGTERM");
    try { await bounded(exited, graceMs, "SIGTERM"); }
    catch {
      child.kill("SIGKILL");
      await bounded(exited, 5000, "SIGKILL reap");
    }
  } finally { child.removeListener("exit", done); child.removeListener("error", done); }
  await groupGone(child);
}
async function groupGone(child: ChildProcess): Promise<void> {
  const pid = privateGroups.get(child);
  if (!pid || process.platform === "win32") return;
  const existing = groupClosures.get(child);
  if (existing) return existing;
  const cleanup = (async () => {
    const expires = performance.now() + 5000;
    for (;;) {
      try { process.kill(-pid, 0); }
      catch (error) { if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ESRCH") return; throw error; }
      const remaining = expires - performance.now();
      if (remaining <= 0) throw Error("proof process-group cleanup timed out after 5000 ms");
      await sleep(Math.min(10, remaining));
    }
  })();
  groupClosures.set(child, cleanup);
  return cleanup;
}
/** @throws partial, invalid or reversed PORT_LO/PORT_HI pair. */
export function portRange(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): string {
  const low = env.PORT_LO, high = env.PORT_HI;
  if (low === undefined && high === undefined) return "0";
  if (!low || !high || !/^\d+$/.test(low) || !/^\d+$/.test(high)
      || Number(low) < 1 || Number(high) > 65535 || Number(low) > Number(high)) {
    throw Error("PORT_LO and PORT_HI must both specify an inclusive range, 1 <= low <= high <= 65535");
  }
  return `${Number(low)}-${Number(high)}`;
}
/** App-local evidence survives harness cleanup of its temporary root. */
/** @throws None; returns the resolved explicit or cwd/logs path. */
export function logsDir(options: Pick<ProofOptions, "cwd" | "logsDir"> = {}): string {
  return resolve(options.cwd ?? ".", options.logsDir ?? "logs");
}
export function logged(command: string, args: readonly string[], options: ProofOptions = {}) {
  const cwd = resolve(options.cwd ?? "."), id = randomUUID();
  const directory = logsDir(options); mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  const logs = { stdout: join(directory, `${id}.stdout.log`), stderr: join(directory, `${id}.stderr.log`) };
  if (options.secret) writeFileSync(logs.stdout, "stdout withheld: secret command (returned only to caller)\n", { flag: "wx", mode: 0o600 });
  const out = options.secret ? undefined : openSync(logs.stdout, "wx", 0o600), err = openSync(logs.stderr, "wx", 0o600);
  const grouped = options.processGroup === true && process.platform !== "win32";
  // Frontends are already detached group leaders with an in-group keeper.
  // Record their group too, so stop/startup cleanup cannot report success
  // before Vite plugins and other inherited descendants have left custody.
  const privateGroup = process.platform !== "win32" && (grouped || options.detached === true);
  const executable = grouped ? process.execPath : command;
  const executableArgs = grouped ? [resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL("./proof-command.js", import.meta.url))), command, ...args] : [...args];

  try { child = spawn(executable, executableArgs, { cwd, detached: grouped || (options.detached ?? false), env: { ...(options.env ?? process.env), SNAPBACK4_PROOF_LAUNCH: id }, stdio: [grouped || options.livenessPipe ? "pipe" : "ignore", options.secret ? "pipe" : out!, err, ...(grouped ? ["ipc" as const] : [])] }); }
  finally { if (out !== undefined) closeSync(out); closeSync(err); }
  if (privateGroup && child.pid) privateGroups.set(child, child.pid);
  // Secret stdout never reaches a file, even briefly. Callers still receive it.
  let stdout = "";
  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
  child.stdout?.on("data", chunk => { stdout += chunk; });
  register(child);
  child.stdin?.on("error", () => {});
  let error: Error | undefined;
  let actualPid = child.pid;
  let actualCode: number | null = null;
  let actualSignal: NodeJS.Signals | null = null;
  let startedResolve!: () => void, startedReject!: (error: Error) => void, startedSettled = false;
  const started = new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => { startedResolve = resolve; startedReject = reject; });
  void started.catch(() => {}); // command() observes close/error instead; host startup awaits this promise.
  const didStart = () => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedResolve(); } };
  const failedStart = (value: unknown) => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedReject(value instanceof Error ? value : Error(String(value))); } };
  if (!grouped) didStart();
  child.on("message", message => {
    const event = message as {type?:string;pid?:number;code?:number|null;signal?:NodeJS.Signals|null;error?:string};
    if (event.type === "started" && typeof event.pid === "number") { actualPid = event.pid; didStart(); }
    if (event.type === "result") { actualCode = event.code ?? null; actualSignal = event.signal ?? null; if (event.error) error = Error(event.error); }
  });
  child.on("error", value => { error = value; failedStart(value); });
  const closed = new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => child.once("close", () => {
    failedStart(error ?? Error("proof command exited before its process-group handshake"));
    groupGone(child).then(resolve,reject);
  }));
  // Hosts use stopChild() as their cleanup join; commands await closed directly.
  // Observe the promise here as well so an early frontend close cannot create
  // an unhandled rejection before its startup catch reaches stopChild().
  void closed.catch(() => {});
  return { child, logs, id, closed, started, pid: () => actualPid, code: () => grouped ? actualCode : child.exitCode, signal: () => grouped ? actualSignal : child.signalCode, stdout: () => options.secret ? stdout : logText(logs.stdout), error: () => error };
}
export const logText = (path: string): string => readFileSync(path, "utf8");
export async function ready(run: ReturnType<typeof logged>, parse: (line: string) => string | undefined, timeoutMs: number): Promise<string> {
  const end = performance.now() + timeoutMs;
  let outAt = 0, errAt = 0;
  while (performance.now() < end) {
    if (run.error()) throw run.error();
    if (run.child.exitCode !== null || run.child.signalCode !== null) {
      throw Error(`proof child exited before ready (${run.child.exitCode ?? run.child.signalCode}); ${run.logs.stderr}\n${logText(run.logs.stderr).slice(-4000)}`);
    }
    for (const [path, offset, stream] of [[run.logs.stdout, outAt, "out"], [run.logs.stderr, errAt, "err"]] as const) {
      const text = logText(path);
      const complete = text.lastIndexOf("\n") + 1;
      for (const line of text.slice(offset, complete).split("\n")) {
        const url = parse(stripVTControlCharacters(line).trim());
        if (url) return url;
      }
      if (stream === "out") outAt = complete; else errAt = complete;
    }
    await sleep(25);
  }
  throw Error(`proof child ready timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms; logs: ${run.logs.stdout}, ${run.logs.stderr}`);
}

const fetchIdentity = async (url: string, timeoutMs: number) => {
  const response = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) });
  return { response, body: await response.json() as Record<string, unknown> };
};
async function nativeHost(verb: "dev" | "serve", prefix: string[], options: ProofOptions): Promise<ProofHost & { personas?: string[] }> {
  const env = { ...process.env, ...options.env }, id = randomUUID();
  const ports = portRange(env), timeout = deadline(options.timeoutMs, 30_000);
  const args = [...(options.args ?? [])];
  if (!args.includes("--port")) args.push("--port", ports);
  const run = logged(resolveBinary(env), [verb, ...prefix, ...args], { ...options, processGroup: true, env: { ...env, SNAPBACK4_PROOF_ID: id, SNAPBACK4_SUPERVISOR_PID: String(process.pid) } });
  try {
    await bounded(run.started, timeout, "proof process-group handshake");
    const url = await ready(run, line => {
      const match = line.match(/^SNAPBACK4_READY verb=(dev|serve) generation=\d+ url=(http:\/\/[^ ]+) pid=(\d+)(?: |$)/);
      if (!match) return;
      if (match[1] !== verb || Number(match[3]) !== run.pid()) throw Error("proof ready identity mismatch");
      return match[2];
    }, timeout);
    const { response, body } = await fetchIdentity(`${url}/auth/config`, timeout);
    if (!response.ok || body.proof_id !== id) throw Error("proof served identity mismatch");
    if (verb === "dev" && body.devDoors === false) process.stderr.write("snapback4: password-only development doors CLOSED (/seed, /dev/*, personas). For shared previews and probe:serve run snapback4 deploy staging --staging, then startServe(\"staging\"); see snapback4 guide staging. Local fixtures require dev --unsafe-dev-doors.\n");
    let personas: string[] = [];
    if (verb === "dev" && body.devDoors !== false) {
      const status = await fetchIdentity(`${url}/dev/status`, timeout);
      if (status.body.pid !== run.pid()) throw Error("proof dev PID mismatch");
      if (!Array.isArray(status.body.personas) || !status.body.personas.every(name => typeof name === "string")) throw Error("proof dev personas missing");
      personas = status.body.personas;
    }
    return { url, ...(verb === "dev" ? { personas } : {}), pid: run.pid()!, logs: run.logs, stop: () => stopChild(run.child, deadline(options.stopTimeoutMs, 5000)) };
  } catch (error) { await stopChild(run.child, deadline(options.stopTimeoutMs, 5000)); throw error; }
}
export interface DevHost extends ProofHost {
  personas: string[];
  /** Read the current authoritative development time, including all clock advances. */
  now(): Promise<number>;
  advance(duration: string, options?: AdvanceOptions): Promise<ClockAdvance>;
  drain(options?: Pick<AdvanceOptions, "eachBoundary" | "allowHeld">): Promise<ClockAdvance>;
  operatorToken(service?: string, days?: number): Promise<string>;
}
/** The array form preserves the former startDev(args) recipe. */
/** @throws invalid port range or conflicting memory flags; child exits, readiness deadline, PID/served identity mismatch, or unavailable dev clock. */
export function startDev(options: ProofOptions | readonly string[] = {}): Promise<DevHost> {
  const opts: ProofOptions = Array.isArray(options) ? { args: options } : options as ProofOptions;
  const args = [...(opts.args ?? [])];
  const persistent = args.some(arg => arg === "--store" || arg.startsWith("--store=") || arg === "--no-memory");
  if (persistent && args.includes("--memory")) throw new TypeError("proof startDev: --memory conflicts with --store/--no-memory");
  // Native persistence is the default. --no-memory remains a consumed explicit alias.
  const host = nativeHost("dev", [], { ...opts, args: args.filter(arg => arg !== "--no-memory") });
  return host.then(host => {
    const operatorToken = async (service = "operator", days = 1) => {
      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(days) || days < 1 || days > 3650) throw Error("proof operatorToken: invalid service or days (1..3650)");
      const port = new URL(host.url).port;
      const result = await cli(["token", "--service", service, "--days", String(days), "--port", port, "--quiet"], opts);
      if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof development operator token refused: ${result.stderr}`);
      const token = result.stdout.trim();
      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(token)) throw Error("proof development operator token malformed");
      return token;
    };
    const clockCall = async (body?: object): Promise<ClockAdvance> => {
      const response = await fetch(`${host.url}/dev/clock/${body ? "advance" : "status"}`, { method: body ? "POST" : "GET", headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${await operatorToken()}`, "content-type": "application/json" }, ...(body ? { body: JSON.stringify(body) } : {}), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 60_000)) });
      const result = await response.json() as Partial<ClockAdvance> & {denied?:{code?:string;message?:string}};
      if (!response.ok || result.denied || !Number.isSafeInteger(result.now)) throw Object.assign(Error(`development clock refused or reply unavailable; inspect before retrying: ${result.denied?.code ?? response.status} ${result.denied?.message ?? ""}`), {report:result});
      const now = result.now!;
      return { now, fired: result.fired ?? [], held: result.held ?? [], maintenancePaused: result.maintenancePaused ?? false, valueOf() { return now; } };
    };
    return { ...host, personas: host.personas!, operatorToken, now: async () => (await clockCall()).now,
      advance: (duration: string, advanceOptions: AdvanceOptions = {}) => {
        if (typeof duration !== "string" || (!/^\+?\d+(ms|s|m|h|d|w)$/.test(duration) || BigInt(duration.replace(/\D/g, "")) === 0n)) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: advance requires a positive whole duration");
        return clockCall({duration, ...advanceOptions});
      },
      drain: (advanceOptions: Pick<AdvanceOptions,"eachBoundary"|"allowHeld"> = {}) => clockCall({duration:"0ms",drain:true,...advanceOptions}),
    };
  });
}

export interface ClockAdvance { now: number; fired: ScheduleOutcome[]; held: ScheduleOutcome[]; maintenancePaused: boolean; valueOf(): number }

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#2-real-staging-accounts — operator authority stays in the existing local store proof; bulk setup refuses production.
/** Starts a release. stop() awaits native exit and kernel store release.
 * @throws E_PROOF_USAGE for missing deployment directory; child exit, readiness deadline or served identity mismatch. stop() rejects bounded cleanup failure. */
export async function startServe(deployDir: string, options: ServeOptions | readonly string[] = {}): Promise<ServeHost> {
  if (typeof deployDir !== "string" || !deployDir.trim()) throw Object.assign(new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: startServe(deployDir, options) requires a deployment directory as its first argument"), { code: "E_PROOF_USAGE" });
  const opts: ServeOptions = Array.isArray(options) ? { args: options } : options as ServeOptions;
  const directory = resolve(opts.cwd ?? ".", deployDir);
  if (opts.clockOffset !== undefined && (typeof opts.clockOffset !== "string" || !/^[+-]?\d+(ms|s|m|h|d|w)$/.test(opts.clockOffset))) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: clockOffset is a signed duration such as +25h");
  if (opts.clockOffset !== undefined && opts.args?.some(arg => arg === "--clock-offset" || arg.startsWith("--clock-offset="))) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: pass clockOffset once");
  const host = await nativeHost("serve", [directory], { ...opts, args: [...(opts.args ?? []), ...(opts.clockOffset === undefined ? [] : ["--clock-offset", opts.clockOffset])] });
  const clockCall = async (body?: object): Promise<ClockAdvance> => {
    const config = await fetchIdentity(`${host.url}/auth/config`, deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 10_000));
    if (!config.response.ok || config.body.environment !== "staging") throw Error("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY: clock controls require a deploy --staging store");
    const clockToken = served.operatorToken("clock");
    const response = await fetch(`${host.url}/dev/clock/${body ? "advance" : "status"}`, { method: body ? "POST" : "GET", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${await clockToken}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, ...(body ? { body: JSON.stringify(body) } : {}), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 60_000)) });
    const result = await response.json() as Partial<ClockAdvance> & { sessionNotice?: string; denied?: { code?: string; message?: string } };
    if (result.sessionNotice) process.stderr.write(`snapback4: ${result.sessionNotice}\n`);
    if (!response.ok || result.denied || !Number.isSafeInteger(result.now)) throw Object.assign(Error(`staging clock refused or reply unavailable; inspect clock and queued work before retrying: ${result.denied?.code ?? response.status} ${result.denied?.message ?? ""}`), { report: result });
    if (body && (!Array.isArray(result.fired) || !Array.isArray(result.held))) throw Error("staging clock reply has no schedule report; inspect clock and queued work before retrying");
    for (const schedule of result.held ?? []) if (schedule.holdCode === "saved-boundary") process.stderr.write(`snapback4: schedule ${schedule.name}: ${schedule.reason}\n`);
    const report: ClockAdvance = { now: result.now!, fired: result.fired ?? [], held: result.held ?? [], maintenancePaused: result.maintenancePaused ?? false, valueOf() { return this.now; } };
    return report;
  };
  // Exit can precede inherited watchdog flock release. The private local
  // barrier observes the same canonical ownership sidecar without writing data.
  let stopping: Promise<void> | undefined;
  const stop = () => stopping ??= (async () => {
    await host.stop();
    const result = await cli(["serve", directory, "--wait-stopped"], {...opts, timeoutMs:6000});
    if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof serve store release failed: ${result.stderr}`);
  })().catch(error => { stopping = undefined; throw error; });
  const served: ServeHost = { ...host, stop,
    now: async () => (await clockCall()).now,
    advance: (duration, options = {}) => {
      if (typeof duration !== "string" || (!/^\+?\d+(ms|s|m|h|d|w)$/.test(duration) || BigInt(duration.replace(/\D/g, "")) === 0n)) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: advance requires a positive whole duration");
      return clockCall({ duration, ...options });
    },
    drain: (options = {}) => clockCall({ duration: "0ms", drain: true, ...options }),
    operatorToken: async (service = "operator", days = 1) => {
      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(days) || days < 1 || days > 3650) throw Error("proof operatorToken: invalid service or days (1..3650)");
      const result = await cli(["token", "--service", service, "--days", String(days), "--release", directory, "--quiet"], opts);
      if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof operator token refused: ${result.stderr}`);
      const token = result.stdout.trim();
      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(token)) throw Error("proof operator token malformed");
      return token;
    },
    seedAccounts: accountOptions => seedAccounts(served, accountOptions),
    provisionAccounts: accountOptions => provisionAccounts(served, accountOptions),
  };
  try {
    if (opts.seedUsers && opts.provisionUsers) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: choose seedUsers for staging or provisionUsers for production");
    if (opts.seedUsers) served.sessions = await served.seedAccounts(opts.seedUsers);
    if (opts.provisionUsers) served.sessions = await served.provisionAccounts(opts.provisionUsers);
    return served;
  }
  catch (error) { await served.stop(); throw error; }
}
async function frontend(kind: "static" | "vite", dir: string, options: ProofOptions): Promise<ProofHost> {
  const env = { ...process.env, ...options.env }, ports = portRange(env), timeout = deadline(options.timeoutMs, 30_000);
  const cwd = resolve(options.cwd ?? ".");
  const directory = resolve(cwd, dir);
  // Vite is resolved from the app, never the proof package's development dependencies.
  const vite = kind === "vite" ? createRequire(resolve(directory, "package.json")).resolve("vite") : "";
  const run = logged(process.execPath, [fileURLToPath(new URL("./proof-host.js", import.meta.url)), kind, directory, ports, vite], { ...options, env, detached: process.platform !== "win32", livenessPipe: true });
  try {
    const url = await ready(run, line => {
      const match = line.match(/^SNAPBACK4_PROOF_READY (\{.*\})$/);
      if (!match) return;
      const data = JSON.parse(match[1]!);
      if (data.pid !== run.child.pid || data.kind !== kind) throw Error("proof frontend PID mismatch");
      return data.url as string;
    }, timeout);
    const response = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeout) });
    if (response.headers.get("x-snapback4-proof") !== String(run.child.pid) + ":" + run.id) throw Error("proof frontend identity mismatch");
    await response.body?.cancel();
    return { url, pid: run.child.pid!, logs: run.logs, stop: () => stopChild(run.child, deadline(options.stopTimeoutMs, 5000)) };
  } catch (error) { await stopChild(run.child, deadline(options.stopTimeoutMs, 5000)); throw error; }
}
/** @throws missing export/index or build script precondition; exhausted ports, readiness deadline or served identity mismatch. */

/** @throws missing Vite dependency/configuration; exhausted ports, readiness deadline or served identity mismatch. */
export function startVite(dir: string, options: ProofOptions = {}): Promise<ProofHost> { return frontend("vite", dir, options); }

## 10. Wave 13: durable evidence and bounded empty clicks (KIT2)

Implementer: KIT2, 2026-10-16, authorized by fix list #3 and H9.
This amendment replaces conflicting §8 defaults; it changes no wire, language,
authorization, adoption, sync, identifier or expiry semantics.

- `renderedText(page,text,{exact=true,within?})` uses Playwright's text matching,
  excludes input/textarea, and supports substring strings and RegExp rows.
  RN-web split nodes require deliberate container scope or `.first()` when
  they represent the same row. `waitForFresh` permits an omitted container;
  its bounded failure includes locator, last count/text and absent/unchanged.
- Logs default to `<cwd>/logs`: H6 deletes the harness TMPDIR, so printing a
  temporary path would not preserve failed evidence. Exact app/ callers whose
  source discovery includes logs choose an explicit artifact directory outside
  that source root. Fresh private files and direct-child custody are unchanged.
  `cli` detects the token verb and captures stdout in memory; `secret:true`
  does the same for cli/command. Secret stdout never touches disk, including
  partial/failed output. A command closes its private secret-stdout read end on
  success/failure so an exited tool's inherited writer cannot pin the driver
  past its deadline; arbitrary descendant process cleanup is still not claimed.
  Stderr remains diagnostic evidence: tools must keep
  secrets off stderr. API results still return stdout to the caller.
- **Historical contract, superseded by LLP 3000.000.000.001 §4:**
  `startDev` appended --memory even with custom arguments, unless --store
  (including --store=...) or --no-memory is explicit. Native store policy is
  unchanged. --no-memory is consumed by the kit to select native dev's default
  persistent store; conflicting --memory refuses. --store, if supplied, remains
  a native flag and its native validation applies (current dev refuses it; use
  --no-memory for cwd/.snapback4/store.sqlite). Browser contexts created by
  `withBrowser` add witness=web to each top-level HTTP(S) document with an init
  script before application scripts, including redirect destinations; no
  production browser or bare Playwright context changes.
- `beginForm` retains trusted click/synchronous-submit provenance and exact
  canonical arguments. An arm with no durable invocation settles failed with
  E_WITNESS_NO_WRITE and message "armed click produced no durable mutation
  (form handler returned early, or the app was not ready)": 1 second after the
  trusted click, immediately on re-arm, or 30 seconds after an abandoned arm.
  A first durable invocation with wrong provenance/operation/arguments remains
  failed/E_WITNESS_UNCLAIMED and still runs normally. A claimed pending write
  has a separate 30-second proof deadline starting at claim (E_WITNESS_SENT);
  arming time never consumes settlement allowance. This is no server refusal.
  Re-arm settles a claimed unsettled observation E_WITNESS_UNCLAIMED, releases
  timers/wrappers/listeners, and never cancels or retries the actual write.
  Four documented terminal paths are sent, app refusal, unclaimed invocation,
  and no invocation; pending custody itself is never proof success.
- `waitForServer(read,accepts,{timeoutMs=30000,label?})` bounds each poll and
  the whole wait, returning the accepted authoritative projection. Its deadline
  names the label and last value. It neither declares settlement nor retries
  writes; callers assert the write's sent receipt first. A read exception
  propagates rather than being mistaken for an unchanged answer.

pass and both baseline controls must fail. Affected proof/witness files run on
Linux and Darwin; no Linux-only inspection is added to the published helper.

orchestration: no SDK delivery/recovery call graph or fault recipe changes.

/** @throws E_STAGING_INPUT for invalid plans; E_STAGING for production/dev hosts; E_STAGING_TIMEOUT, E_STAGING_SIGNUP or E_STAGING_PROVISION for incomplete setup. Partial accounts/grants may exist; inspect or discard the staging store before retrying. */
async function accounts(host: Pick<ServeHost, "url" | "operatorToken">, options: SeedAccountsOptions, environment: "staging" | "production"): Promise<StagingSessions> {
  // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — custom argument keys override defaults; the seat grants no extra authority.
  const service = options.service ?? "operator";
  const roles = Object.entries(options.roles), timeout = options.timeoutMs ?? 300_000;
  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(timeout) || timeout < 1 || !roles.length || roles.some(([role, n]) => !/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/.test(role) || !Number.isSafeInteger(n) || n < 1)
      || roles.reduce((sum, [, n]) => sum + n, 0) > 100 || !/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*$/.test(options.provision?.name ?? "")) {
    throw Error("E_STAGING_INPUT: provide 1..100 accounts across named roles, a mutation handle and a positive timeoutMs");
  }
  const end = performance.now() + timeout;
  const partial = environment === "staging" ? "inspect or discard this staging deployment" : "inspect partial production accounts/grants before retrying";
  const remaining = () => {
    const ms = Math.ceil(end - performance.now());
    if (ms <= 0) throw Error(`E_STAGING_TIMEOUT: setup incomplete; partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
    return ms;
  };
  const request = (path: string, init?: RequestInit) => fetch(host.url + path, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(Math.min(remaining(), 30_000)) });
  const config = await request("/auth/config");
  const identity = await config.json();
  if (!config.ok || identity.environment !== environment || identity.development !== false || !identity.password) {
    throw Error(environment === "staging"
      ? "E_STAGING: account seeding requires serve on a fresh deploy --staging with password identity; production and dev refuse before creating users"
      : "E_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNTS: account provisioning requires serve on a production deploy with password identity; staging and dev refuse before creating users");
  }
  const operator = await host.operatorToken(service);
  if (environment === "production") {
    const response = await request("/schema", { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${operator}` } }), schema = await response.json();
    const named = response.ok && Array.isArray(schema.service_identities) && schema.service_identities.includes(`service:${service}`);
    if (!named) process.stderr.write(`snapback4: WARNING minted service:${service}, but the served schema reports no explicit positive authorization mention for that service identity; rules still decide every operation and provisionAccounts(${options.provision.name}) will likely refuse.\n`);
  }
  const sessions: StagingSessions = Object.create(null);
  for (const [role, count] of roles) {
    sessions[role] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const email = `${environment}-${role}-${randomUUID()}@example.test`, password = randomBytes(24).toString("base64url");
      const {json: reply} = await identityRequest(host.url + "/auth/signup", {
        method:"POST", headers:{"content-type":"application/json"}, body:JSON.stringify({email,password}),
      }, fetch, {timeoutMs:remaining()}).catch(error => {
        if ((error as {code?: string})?.code === "E_IDENTITY_TIMEOUT") throw Error(`E_STAGING_TIMEOUT: signup deadline expired; partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
        remaining(); throw error;
      });
      if ((reply.denied as {code?:string} | undefined)?.code === "E_RATE_LIMIT") {
        throw Error("E_STAGING_TIMEOUT: identity retry budget exhausted; increase timeoutMs or inspect partial accounts/grants before retrying");
      }
      const session = reply.session as {principal?:string;kind?:string;token?:string;expiresAt?:number} | undefined;
      if (typeof session?.principal !== "string" || typeof session.token !== "string" || typeof session.expiresAt !== "number" || session.kind !== "user") {
        throw Error(`E_STAGING_SIGNUP: signup refused (${(reply.denied as {code?:string} | undefined)?.code ?? "invalid reply"}); partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
      }
      const account: StagingAccount = { kind: session.kind, role, email, password, principal: session.principal, token: session.token, expiresAt: session.expiresAt };
      const args = { principal: account.principal, role, ...options.args?.(account) };
      const response = await request(`/m/${options.provision.name}`, { method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json", authorization: `Bearer ${operator}` }, body: JSON.stringify({ id: randomUUID(), args }) });
      const result = await response.json();
      if (!response.ok || result.state !== "sent") throw Error(`E_STAGING_PROVISION: ${options.provision.name} refused (${result.why?.code ?? result.denied?.code ?? "invalid reply"}); partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
      sessions[role]!.push(account);
    }
  }
  return sessions;
}

//! A process-local clock for development and explicitly classified staging stores.
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — preserve expiry tests and tell callers how to recover.
pub(crate) const SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Time travel also advances session expiry and unplaced-upload collection: seven-day password sessions may now be expired. Sign in again after the jump and upload unplaced bytes after it; never replay an ambiguous clock advance.";

pub(crate) const PRESERVED_SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Authenticated development and staging sessions keep their remaining lifetime across this jump; sessions:expire explicitly tests credential expiry. Unplaced uploads still age. Never replay an ambiguous advance.";

const MAX_TIME: i64 = snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX;

pub fn input(message: impl Into<String>) -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INPUT", "clock", message).guide("clock") }
pub fn release() -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY", "clock", "clock controls require dev or a deploy --staging store; production always uses wall time").guide("clock") }

/// Isolated time tests stay inside an assigned range, or request a free port.
pub(crate) fn isolated_command() -> String {
    isolated_range(std::env::var("PORT_LO").ok().as_deref(), std::env::var("PORT_HI").ok().as_deref())
}
fn isolated_range(lo: Option<&str>, hi: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match (lo.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok()), hi.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())) {
        (Some(lo), Some(hi)) if lo > 0 && hi >= lo => format!("dev --memory --port {lo}-{hi} within the current range"),
        _ => "dev --memory --port 0".into(),
    }
}

pub fn duration(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if text.starts_with('-') { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
    let text = text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text);
    let split = text.bytes().position(|b| !b.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(text.len());
    let (number, unit) = text.split_at(split);
    let multiplier = match unit { "ms" => 1, "s" => 1_000, "m" => 60_000, "h" => 3_600_000, "d" => 86_400_000, "w" => 604_800_000, _ => 0 };
    number.parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(multiplier)).filter(|n| *n > 0 && *n <= MAX_TIME)
        .ok_or_else(|| input("expected a positive whole duration with ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as +25h"))
}

pub fn offset(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if let Some(rest) = text.strip_prefix('-') { duration(rest).map(|n| -n) } else { duration(text) }
}

fn time(value: Option<i64>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    value.filter(|n| (0..=MAX_TIME).contains(n)).ok_or_else(|| input("time must be Unix milliseconds in 0..9007199254740991; choose a smaller time or duration"))
}

pub fn run_now(text: Option<&String>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    let now = snapback4_core::now_ms();
    match text {
        None => Ok(now),
        Some(text) if text.starts_with('+') => time(now.checked_add(duration(text)?)),
        Some(text) => time(text.parse().ok()),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Clock {
    dev: bool,
    base: i64,
    offset: i64,
    started: Instant,
    epoch: String,
    revision: u64,
    #[cfg(test)]
    frozen: bool,
}

impl Clock {
    pub fn new(dev: bool, offset: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        if !dev && offset != 0 { return Err(release()); }
        Ok(Self { dev, offset, base: time(snapback4_core::now_ms().checked_add(offset))?, started: Instant::now(),
            epoch: snapback4_core::ids::mint(snapback4_core::now_ms(), &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?, revision: 0, #[cfg(test)] frozen: false })
    }
    pub fn staging(offset: i64, floor: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        let mut clock = Self::new(true, offset)?;
        let delta = floor.saturating_sub(clock.now()).max(0);
        if delta > 0 { clock.advance(delta)?; }
        Ok(clock)
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn freeze(&mut self, now: i64) { self.base = now; self.frozen = true; }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        #[cfg(test)] if self.frozen { return self.base; }
        if !self.dev { return snapback4_core::now_ms(); }
        self.base.saturating_add(self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64).min(MAX_TIME)
    }
    /// Identifies samples taken before/after a restart or deliberate clock jump.
    pub fn offset(&self) -> i64 { self.offset }
    pub fn revision(&self) -> String { format!("{}:{}", self.epoch, self.revision) }
    pub fn presence_now(&self) -> i64 {
        // Production grace is elapsed real time, unaffected by wall-clock corrections.
        if self.dev { self.now() } else { self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64 }
    }
    /// Back to wall time: the offset `--clock-offset` and every advance added
    /// is dropped (a development reset's `{"clock":"reset"}`).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = 0;
        self.base = snapback4_core::now_ms();
        self.started = Instant::now();
        #[cfg(test)] { self.frozen = false; }
        Ok(self.base)
    }
    pub fn advance(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        if milliseconds <= 0 { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
        let next = time(self.now().checked_add(milliseconds))?;
        let offset = self.offset.checked_add(milliseconds).ok_or_else(|| input("cumulative clock offset overflow"))?;
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = offset;
        self.base = next;
        self.started = Instant::now();
        Ok(next)
    }
}

/// The control CLI only talks to a loopback dev host. It does not open its store.
pub fn command(options: &crate::verbs::Options) -> i32 {
    let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
        let draining = options.positionals == ["drain"];
        if !draining && (options.positionals.len() != 2 || options.positionals[0] != "advance") {
            return Err(input(format!("usage: {}", crate::cli_flags::synopsis("clock"))).to_string());
        }
        let duration_text = if draining { "0ms" } else { options.positionals[1].as_str() };
        if !draining { duration(duration_text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; }
        let release_path = options.flags.get("release").map(|dir| std::path::PathBuf::from(dir).join("store.sqlite"));
        if release_path.is_some() && options.flags.contains_key("port") { return Err("clock --release does not accept --port".into()); }
        let (address, instance, token) = if let Some(path) = &release_path {
            let store = snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::open_read_only(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if store.deployment_environment().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(release().to_string()); }
            let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(path).ok_or("staging clock requires a running serve")?;
            let session = crate::serve::token::mint_live(path, "clock", 1).map_err(|(_,error)|error)?;
            (address,None,Some(session.token))
        } else {
            let (address,instance)=crate::verbs::dev_address(options)?;
            // A production listener has no development-token registry entry.
            // Ask its read-only clock door first so the CLI preserves the
            // server's actionable refusal instead of failing token discovery.
            if let Ok((_, status)) = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/clock/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5))
                && status["denied"]["code"] == "E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY"
            {
                return Err(release().to_string());
            }
            let token=crate::verbs::mint_for_dev(address,"operator",1)?;
            (address,instance,Some(token))
        };
        let mut body = serde_json::json!({"duration":duration_text,"eachBoundary":options.flags.contains_key("each-boundary"), "drain":!options.flags.contains_key("no-drain"), "allowHeld":options.flags.contains_key("allow-held")});
        if options.flags.contains_key("expire-sessions") { body["sessions"] = "expire".into(); }
        if draining && options.flags.contains_key("no-drain") { return Err(input("clock drain does not accept --no-drain").to_string()); }
        let body = body.to_string();
        // The common HTTP/1.0 exchange is EOF-delimited and bounds replies at
        // 64 MiB, enough for the preflight's complete explicit window report.
        let response = if release_path.is_some() {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_authorized(address,"POST","/dev/clock/advance",None,token.as_deref(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        } else {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_dev_authorized(address,"/dev/clock/advance",instance.as_deref(),token.as_deref().unwrap(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        };
        let (status, json) = response.map_err(|error| {
            let evidence = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5)).ok()
                .map(|(_, status)| format!("now={}, skewMs={}", status["now"], status["skewMs"]))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "clock status unavailable".into());
            format!("clock advance reply failed at {address}: {error}; time may already have advanced ({evidence}); inspect /dev/status and queued work before retrying; for an isolated dev pass --port N")
        })?;
        if let Some(notice) = json["sessionNotice"].as_str() { eprintln!("clock: {notice}"); }
        if let Some(held) = json["held"].as_array() {
            for schedule in held.iter().filter(|s| s["holdCode"] == "saved-boundary") {
                eprintln!("clock: schedule {}: {}", schedule["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"), schedule["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or("held"));
            }
        }
        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
            if json.get("now").is_some() {
                eprintln!("clock: incomplete advance report (time already moved): {}", serde_json::json!({"now":json["now"],"fired":json["fired"],"held":json["held"]}));
            }
            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
        }
        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
        Ok(json.to_string())
    })();
    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
}

import type { Session } from "./auth.ts";
import { isReadToken } from "./read-token.ts";

/** Authenticated development and staging return this exact bearer's current live lifetime.
 * Matching the dispatch bearer is the caller's responsibility. Same-bearer
 * preservation is monotonic, so a delayed old reply cannot undo a jump. */
export function reconciledTiming(session: Session, response: Response): Session {
  if (response.headers.get("x-snapback-session-timing") !== "staging") return session;
  const expiry = Number(response.headers.get("x-snapback-session-expires"));
  const capText = response.headers.get("x-snapback-session-cap");
  const cap = capText === null ? undefined : Number(capText);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(expiry) || expiry <= 0) return session;
  const read = isReadToken(session.token);
  if (read && (cap === undefined || !Number.isSafeInteger(cap) || cap < expiry)) return session;
  if (!read && cap !== undefined) return session;
  const expiresAt = Math.max(session.expiresAt, expiry);
  const capExpiresAt = cap === undefined ? undefined : Math.max(session.capExpiresAt ?? 0, cap);
  if (expiresAt === session.expiresAt && capExpiresAt === session.capExpiresAt) return session;
  return { ...session, expiresAt, ...(capExpiresAt === undefined ? {} : { capExpiresAt }) };
}

export function requestMatchesSession(request: { url: string; authorization: string | null }, base: string, session: Session): boolean {
  return (request.url === base || request.url.startsWith(base + "/")) && request.authorization === `Bearer ${session.token}`;
}

/** Expired local metadata may be superseded by a preserving development or staging jump.
 * Read-only probing creates no session and never widens or refreshes one. */
export async function restoreStagingTiming(base: string, session: Session, fetcher: typeof fetch): Promise<Session | null> {
  const aborter = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => aborter.abort(), 10_000);
  (timer as { unref?: () => void }).unref?.();
  try {
    const response = await fetcher(`${base}/probe?scope=1`, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${session.token}` }, signal: aborter.signal });
    if (!response.ok) return null;
    const next = reconciledTiming(session, response);
    const stamp = Number(response.headers.get("x-snapback-time"));
    if (next === session || !Number.isSafeInteger(stamp) || next.expiresAt <= stamp) return null;
    // Consume the bounded ordinary probe body before blessing restoration.
    const { readResponse } = await import("./http-response.ts");
    const body = await readResponse(response);
    return body.ok === true && body.viewer === session.principal && body.scope === (isReadToken(session.token) ? "read" : "full") ? next : null;
  } catch { return null; }
  finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
}

//! Exact service principals named by compiled authorization facts.
use snapback4_core::{
    Value,
    ir::{BinaryOp, Expr, Input, Stmt},
    schema::{RuleExpr, RuleTerm},
};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

fn principal(value: &Value) -> Option<&str> {
    match value {
        Value::Id(value) => value
            .strip_prefix("service:")
            .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
            .map(|_| value.as_str()),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn rule(rule: &RuleExpr, seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>, positive: bool) {
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Viewer, RuleTerm::Literal(value))
        | RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Literal(value), RuleTerm::Viewer)
            if positive =>
        {
            if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
                seats.insert(value.into());
            }
        }
        RuleExpr::And(rules) | RuleExpr::Or(rules) => rules
            .iter()
            .for_each(|rule| self::rule(rule, seats, positive)),
        RuleExpr::Not(rule) => self::rule(rule, seats, !positive),
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn expression(expr: &Expr, seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>, positive: bool) {
    match expr {
        Expr::Binary {
            op: BinaryOp::Eq | BinaryOp::SameValueZero,
            left,
            right,
        } => match (&**left, &**right, positive) {
            (Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), Expr::Literal(value), true)
            | (Expr::Literal(value), Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), true) => {
                if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
                    seats.insert(value.into());
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        },
        Expr::Binary {
            op: BinaryOp::And | BinaryOp::Or,
            left,
            right,
        } => {
            expression(left, seats, positive);
            expression(right, seats, positive);
        }
        Expr::Unary {
            op: snapback4_core::ir::UnaryOp::Not,
            value,
        } => expression(value, seats, !positive),
        Expr::Block { body, value } => {
            statements(body, seats);
            expression(value, seats, positive);
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn statements(body: &[Stmt], seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {
    for statement in body {
        match statement {
            Stmt::Require { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
            Stmt::If {
                then_body,
                else_body,
                ..
            } => {
                statements(then_body, seats);
                statements(else_body, seats);
            }
            Stmt::For { body, .. } => statements(body, seats),
            Stmt::Check { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
            Stmt::WriteTarget {
                condition: Some(condition),
                ..
            } => statements(&condition.setup, seats),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — minted seats stay ordinary principals; this is advisory schema evidence, never a grant.
pub(crate) fn collect(bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    let mut seats = BTreeSet::new();
    for table in bound.schema.tables.values() {
        for rule in [
            &table.rules.read,
            &table.rules.insert,
            &table.rules.update,
            &table.rules.delete,
        ] {
            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
        }
        for rule in table.column_reads.values() {
            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
        }
    }
    for program in &bound.programs {
        statements(&program.program.body, &mut seats);
    }
    seats.extend(
        bound
            .schema
            .schedules
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|schedule| schedule.service.clone()),
    );
    seats.extend(
        bound
            .schema
            .routes
            .values()
            .filter_map(|route| route.service.clone()),
    );
    seats
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#4-staging-clock — staging grants clock control, never fixture or persona authority.
pub(super) fn staging(shared: &Shared) -> Result<bool, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    shared.engine.call(|engine, _| engine.store().deployment_environment().ok().flatten().as_deref() == Some("staging"))
}
fn clock_service(request: &Request, shared: &Shared) -> Result<Option<String>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — real-user dev clock authority is independent of fixture doors.
    if shared.personas {
        match super::session_identity::principal_of(request,shared) {
            Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind == "service" && principal == "service:operator" => return Ok(Some(principal)),
            _ if shared.dev_doors() && crate::auth::bearer_token(request).is_err() => return Ok(None),
            _ => return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "development clock control requires a full service:operator token").guide("clock")),
        }
    }
    if !staging(shared)? { return Err(crate::dev_clock::release()); }
    match super::session_identity::principal_of(request,shared) {
        Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind == "service" && principal.starts_with("service:") => Ok(Some(principal)),
        _ => Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "staging clock control requires a full service token").guide("clock")),
    }
}
fn checkpoint_clock(engine: &mut snapback4_core::Engine, delta: i64, before: i64, preserve: bool, checkpoint: &snapback4_core::metadata::StagingClock) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let result = engine.checkpoint_staging_clock_at(delta, before, preserve, checkpoint);
    #[cfg(feature = "postgres")]
    if matches!(result, Err(RuntimeError::CommitOutcomeUnknown(_))) { crate::lifecycle::uncertain_clock_commit(); }
    result
}
fn incomplete_report(cause: &snapback4_core::Refusal) -> snapback4_core::Refusal {
    snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_REPORT_INCOMPLETE", "clock",
        format!("clock already advanced; report incomplete ({cause}); inspect clock or use clock drain (0ms); do not replay the advance"))
        .guide("clock")
}
fn advance_error(error: &snapback4_core::Refusal, published: Option<i64>, milliseconds: i64) -> (u16, serde_json::Value) {
    match published {
        Some(now) => (500, json!({"now":now,"advancedMs":milliseconds,"reportIncomplete":true,"denied":incomplete_report(error)})),
        None => (refusal_status(error, 400), json!({"denied":refusal_json(error)})),
    }
}
