// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — declared table renames preserve Ref inputs; additive result fields are notes.
use crate::{Bound, BoundProgram, types::Ty};
use snapback4_core::ir::{ArgType as A, ProgramKind};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

/// Conservative input-domain inclusion: every value accepted by old is accepted by new.
pub fn accepts(old: &A, new: &A) -> bool {
    accepts_in(old,new,None,None)
}

fn accepts_in(old: &A, new: &A, old_bound: Option<&Bound>, new_bound: Option<&Bound>) -> bool {
    if old==new {return true;}
    match (old,new) {
        (A::Optional(a),A::Optional(b))=>accepts_in(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
        (A::Optional(_),_)=>false,
        (a,A::Optional(b))=>accepts_in(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
        (A::Ref{table:old},A::Ref{table:new})=>new_bound.is_some_and(|bound|bound.schema.table_renames.get(new)==Some(old))
            && old_bound.is_some_and(|bound|bound.schema.table(old).is_some()),
        (A::Text{min:a,max:b,format:af},A::Text{min:c,max:d,format:bf})=>c<=a && d>=b && (bf.is_none() || af==bf),
        (A::IntRange{..},A::Int)=>true,
        (A::IntRange{min:a,max:b},A::IntRange{min:c,max:d})=>c<=a && d>=b,
        (A::Enum{variants:a},A::Enum{variants:b})=>a.iter().all(|v|b.contains(v)),
        (A::Bytes{max:a},A::Bytes{max:b}) | (A::Image{max:a},A::Image{max:b}) |
        (A::Video{max:a},A::Video{max:b})=>b>=a,
        (A::Json{max_bytes:a},A::Json{max_bytes:b})=>b>=a,
        (A::File{max:a,types:at},A::File{max:b,types:bt})=>b>=a && snapback4_core::assets::FILE_TYPES.iter().all(|t|!snapback4_core::assets::file_accepts(at,t)||snapback4_core::assets::file_accepts(bt,t)),
        (A::List{..}|A::ListRange{..},A::List{..}|A::ListRange{..})=> {
            let parts=|t:&A|match t {A::List{of,max}=>(0,*max,of.clone()),A::ListRange{of,min,max}=>(*min,*max,of.clone()),_=>unreachable!()};
            let (a,b,at)=parts(old);let(c,d,bt)=parts(new);
            c<=a && d>=b && match(at,bt){(_,None)=>true,(Some(a),Some(b))=>accepts_in(&a,&b,old_bound,new_bound),_=>false}
        }
        _=>false,
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ResultChange { Same, Additive, Changed }

fn combine(fields: impl IntoIterator<Item=ResultChange>, extra: bool) -> ResultChange {
    let mut additive=extra;
    for field in fields {
        match field {ResultChange::Changed=>return ResultChange::Changed,ResultChange::Additive=>additive=true,ResultChange::Same=>{}}
    }
    if additive {ResultChange::Additive} else {ResultChange::Same}
}

fn table_fields(name: &str, bound: &Bound) -> Option<BTreeMap<String,String>> {
    let schema=bound.schema.public_projection();
    let table=schema.tables.get(name)?;
    Some(table.columns.iter().filter(|(n,_)|!table.engine_field(n)).map(|(n,t)|(n.clone(),format!("{t:?};private={};constraints={:?}",table.read_optional(n),table.constraints.iter().filter(|c|matches!(c,snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Text{field,..} if field==n)).collect::<Vec<_>>()))).collect())
}

fn map_change<T>(old: &BTreeMap<String,T>, new: &BTreeMap<String,T>, compare: impl Fn(&T,&T)->ResultChange) -> ResultChange {
    combine(old.iter().map(|(name,old)|new.get(name).map(|new|compare(old,new)).unwrap_or(ResultChange::Changed)),new.len()>old.len())
}

fn result_change(old: &Ty, new: &Ty, old_bound: &Bound, new_bound: &Bound) -> ResultChange {
    if result(old,old_bound)==result(new,new_bound) {return ResultChange::Same;}
    match (old,new) {
        (Ty::Optional(a),Ty::Optional(b))|(Ty::Omittable(a),Ty::Omittable(b))
        |(Ty::List(a,_),Ty::List(b,_))|(Ty::Collection(a,_),Ty::Collection(b,_))=>result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
        (Ty::Object(a)|Ty::RowShape(a)|Ty::RowObject(a),Ty::Object(b)|Ty::RowShape(b)|Ty::RowObject(b))=>map_change(a,b,|a,b|result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound)),
        (Ty::Row(a),Ty::Row(b)) | (Ty::WriteRow(a),Ty::WriteRow(b)) | (Ty::Page(a,_),Ty::Page(b,_)) if a==b=>{
            let (Some(a),Some(b))=(table_fields(a,old_bound),table_fields(b,new_bound)) else{return ResultChange::Changed;};
            combine(a.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if b.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),b.len()>a.len())
        }
        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
    }
}

fn action_result_change(old: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>, new: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>) -> ResultChange {
    match (old,new) {
        (None,None)=>ResultChange::Same,
        (Some(old),Some(new))=>combine(old.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if new.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),new.len()>old.len()),
        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
    }
}

pub fn is_note(line: &str) -> bool { line.contains(": RESULT NOTE:") }

fn result(ty: &Ty, bound: &Bound) -> String {
    match ty {
        Ty::Row(name)|Ty::WriteRow(name)|Ty::Page(name,_)=> {
            let schema=bound.schema.public_projection();
            if let Some(table)=schema.tables.get(name) {
                let fields: BTreeMap<_,_>=table.columns.iter().filter(|(n,_)|!table.engine_field(n)).map(|(n,t)|(n,format!("{t:?};private={};constraints={:?}",table.read_optional(n),table.constraints.iter().filter(|c|matches!(c,snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Text{field,..} if field==n)).collect::<Vec<_>>()))).collect();
                let kind=match ty {Ty::Row(..)=>"row",Ty::WriteRow(..)=>"write-row",Ty::Page(..)=>"page",_=>unreachable!()};
                format!("{kind}:{name}:{fields:?}")
            } else {format!("{ty:?}")}
        }
        Ty::Optional(t)=>format!("optional {}",result(t,bound)),
        Ty::Omittable(t)=>format!("omittable {}",result(t,bound)),
        Ty::List(t,_)|Ty::Collection(t,_)=>format!("list {}",result(t,bound)),
        Ty::Object(fields)|Ty::RowShape(fields)|Ty::RowObject(fields)=>format!("object {:?}",fields.iter().map(|(n,t)|(n,result(t,bound))).collect::<BTreeMap<_,_>>()),
        Ty::Text(max)=>format!("text<={max}"),
        _=>format!("{ty:?}"),
    }
}

fn refusals(p: &BoundProgram) -> Vec<String> {
    fn walk(v: &serde_json::Value, out: &mut Vec<String>) {
        match v {
            serde_json::Value::Object(o)=> {
                if let Some(r)=o.get("Require") {out.push(format!("{}:{}",r["code"],r["message"]));}
                for v in o.values(){walk(v,out);}
            }
            serde_json::Value::Array(a)=>for v in a{walk(v,out);},
            _=>{}
        }
    }
    let mut out=Vec::new();walk(&serde_json::to_value(&p.program.body).unwrap(),&mut out);out
}

/// Reports are advisory: compatibility cannot license calls or prove unchanged behavior.
pub fn compare(old: &Bound, new: &Bound, label: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut lines=Vec::new();
    for before in old.programs.iter().filter(|p|p.program.kind!=ProgramKind::Job) {
        let name=&before.program.name;
        let prefix=format!("old-client compatibility ({label}), operation {name}");
        let Some(after)=new.programs.iter().find(|p|p.program.name==*name) else {
            lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed operation; old calls get E_OP; keep `alias {name} = replacement` for a same-module query/mutation, or retain a wrapper"));continue;
        };
        if before.program.kind!=after.program.kind {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: operation kind changed; retain the old endpoint kind"));continue;}
        let rename_candidate = |new_kind: &A| before.program.args.iter().find(|(old_name, old_kind)|
            !after.program.args.contains_key(*old_name) && !after.program.arg_aliases.contains_key(*old_name)
                && accepts_in(old_kind,new_kind,Some(old),Some(new)));
        let mut warned_renames=BTreeSet::new();
        for (arg,kind) in &after.program.args {
            if before.program.args.contains_key(arg) { continue; }
            if let Some((old_arg,old_kind))=before.program.args.iter().find(|(old,_)|after.program.arg_aliases.get(*old)==Some(arg)) {
                if !accepts_in(old_kind,kind,Some(old),Some(new)) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: aliased argument {old_arg} → {arg} narrows the old input domain ({old_kind:?} → {kind:?}); retain the old input domain or a compatible wrapper"));}
            } else if !matches!(kind,A::Optional(_)) {
                if let Some((old,_))=rename_candidate(kind) {
                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: required argument {old} appears renamed to {arg}; old calls get E_INPUT; declare `{arg}: <new type> alias {old}` if it is the same value, or retain a compatible wrapper"));
                    warned_renames.insert(old.clone());
                } else {
                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: clients calling without new required argument {arg} get E_INPUT; give {arg} a fitting `default <literal>` or retain a compatible wrapper"));
                }
            }
        }
        for (arg,kind) in &before.program.args {
            match after.program.args.get(arg) {
                None if after.program.arg_aliases.contains_key(arg)=>{
                    let next=&after.program.args[&after.program.arg_aliases[arg]];
                    if !accepts_in(kind,next,Some(old),Some(new)){lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: aliased argument {arg} retyped or narrowed ({kind:?} → {next:?}); retain its old input domain"));}
                },
                None if warned_renames.contains(arg)=>{},
                None=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed argument {arg}; old calls sending it get E_INPUT; retain `{arg}: <old type> deprecated` on a query/mutation")),
                Some(next) if !accepts_in(kind,next,Some(old),Some(new))=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: argument {arg} retyped or narrowed ({kind:?} → {next:?}); old values may get E_INPUT; retain the old input domain or a compatible wrapper")),
                _=>{}
            }
        }
        for (alias,canonical) in &before.program.arg_aliases {
            let old_kind=&before.program.args[canonical];
            let next=after.program.args.get(alias).or_else(||after.program.arg_aliases.get(alias).and_then(|name|after.program.args.get(name)));
            match next {
                None=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed argument alias {alias}; old calls sending it get E_INPUT; retain its alias or a compatible wrapper")),
                Some(kind) if !accepts_in(old_kind,kind,Some(old),Some(new))=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: argument alias {alias} retyped or narrowed ({old_kind:?} → {kind:?}); retain its old input domain")),
                _=>{}
            }
        }
        let mut positions:BTreeMap<String,String>=BTreeMap::new();
        for canonical in before.program.args.keys() {
            for spelling in std::iter::once(canonical).chain(before.program.arg_aliases.iter().filter_map(|(alias,target)|(target==canonical).then_some(alias))) {
                let target=after.program.args.contains_key(spelling).then_some(spelling).or_else(||after.program.arg_aliases.get(spelling));
                if let Some(target)=target {
                    if let Some(prior)=positions.insert(target.clone(),canonical.clone())&&prior!=*canonical {
                        lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: independent arguments {prior} and {canonical} now share {target}; old calls containing both positions get E_INPUT; retain separate arguments or a compatible wrapper"));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        for (table,before_table) in old.schema.visible_tables() {
            let Some(after_table)=new.schema.table(table) else { continue; };
            if !snapback4_core::ir::read_sites(&before.program).iter().any(|site|site.table==*table)
                && !snapback4_core::ir::write_tables(&before.program).iter().any(|(name,_)|name==table) { continue; }
            for field in before_table.columns.keys().filter(|f|!before_table.read_optional(f)&&after_table.read_optional(f)) {
                lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: {table}.{field} is now audience-optional; handle an omitted row property or a null explicit scalar before adopting the new column read rule"));
            }
        }
        let action_change=action_result_change(old.schema.action_specs.get(name).and_then(|s|s.returns.as_ref()),new.schema.action_specs.get(name).and_then(|s|s.returns.as_ref()));
        let typed_change=result_change(&before.result,&after.result,old,new);
        let change=combine([action_change,typed_change],false);
        match change {
            ResultChange::Additive=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT NOTE: result shape added fields while preserving prior fields and domains; old clients may ignore the additions")),
            ResultChange::Changed=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: result shape/value domain changed; preserve the old projection/domain or introduce a new operation before retiring old clients")),
            ResultChange::Same=>{},
        }
        let old_domains=crate::result_domains::signature(before,old);
        let new_domains=crate::result_domains::signature(after,new);
        // A domain introduced only for a newly returned field is covered by
        // the additive result note. Existing or removed domains still need review.
        let changed:Vec<_>=old_domains.keys().collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>().into_iter().filter(|key|old_domains.get(*key)!=new_domains.get(*key)).cloned().collect();
        if !changed.is_empty() {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: declared source domains consumed by this operation changed: {}; results or refusals may change even when the TypeScript type stays number/string; preserve the old domains or verify old-client handling",changed.join(", ")));}
        if refusals(before)!=refusals(after) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: BEHAVIOR REVIEW: refusal codes/messages changed ({:?} → {:?}); verify intended denials separately from input breaks",refusals(before),refusals(after)));}
    }
    lines
}

/// Human result advice groups source columns across operations. JSON keeps compare().
pub fn compact(lines:&[String])->Vec<String>{
    use std::collections::BTreeSet;
    let mut out=Vec::new();let mut groups=BTreeMap::<String,BTreeSet<String>>::new();
    for line in lines {
        let Some((prefix,detail))=line.split_once(": RESULT REVIEW: ") else {out.push(line.clone());continue};
        let operation=prefix.rsplit_once("operation ").map(|(_,name)|name).unwrap_or("unknown");
        if let Some((_,columns))=detail.split_once("declared source domains consumed by this operation changed: ") {
            for column in columns.split(';').next().unwrap_or(columns).split(", "){groups.entry(column.into()).or_default().insert(operation.into());}
        }else{groups.entry(detail.into()).or_default().insert(operation.into());}
    }
    for(detail,ops)in groups{out.push(format!("old-client compatibility: RESULT REVIEW: {detail}; operations [{}]; verify old-client handling (full per-operation evidence in --json)",ops.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")));}
    out
}

rules/RULES.md
# Rules

**Snapback 2 optimizes the edit-to-verified loop — the agent's building an app on it, and ours building it.**

Speed is the constraint. Everything below exists to keep the edit-to-verified loop short
and to stop this repository accreting apparatus faster than anyone can remove it. These
rules bind `snapback2/` and the LLPs numbered 1000 and up; Snapback 1 is baselined, not
exempt, and its numbers may only fall.

Each rule is **[check]** (enforced by `caps`) or **[review]** (enforced by a human).

## Budgets — every budget is a trade, not a limit

- **5 blocking checks, 60s total.** A sixth requires deleting one, in the same PR. **[check]**
- **59 documents in the working set** (`llp/current/`). Today's count. A 60th requires
  archiving one — which is just removing the link. Snapback 2 aims to leave this at 15;
  Snapback 1's links are archived at promotion. **[check]**
- **12 documents in the foundation** (`llp/foundation/`). **[check]**
- **This file: 700 words.** If it grows, something becomes a check or stops being a rule. **[check]**
- **1,500 lines per source file, baseline 204.** Generated files exempt — and generated
  files are built, not committed; so are benchmark run records under `benchmarks/runs/`,
  which are evidence, not source. The baseline is Snapback 1's oversize count on the day
  the rule landed; it may not grow, and `snapback2/` contributes zero to it. **[check]**

## Blocking checks

`caps` · `ref-check` · `snapback2/scripts/test.sh` · `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs --check` · `check-inventories`

## Loop shape

- **Every check reports all failures in one run.** Fail-fast is banned. **[check]**
- **Nothing blocks on anything slower than 60 seconds.** Slow verification runs on a
  schedule, attributed to the breaking commit, and files a bounded set of issues. **[review]**
- **Fix loops get 3 rounds.** Then stop: escalate to a human or descope. **[review]**

## Time budgets

Tracked every run of `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs` (appends `snapback2/metrics/loop.jsonl`).
A regression is a P0 with a name on it.

| | budget |
|---|---|
| Incremental rebuild after a one-line edit | 15s |
| Test what you just changed | 30s |
| Blocking gate suite | 60s |
| Full build, warm cache | 5 min |
| **`snapback2 check` on a program (the agent's product latency)** | **1s** |
| **`snapback2 doctor` boot-to-ready** | **0.5s** |

## Scope

- **`NOT-DOING.md` is binding.** Moving something onto the doing-list means writing why
  and taking something off. **[review]**
- **Delete; don't deprecate.** No compat shims or migration paths before promotion. **[review]**
- **Nothing is compiled, transpiled, or generated at runtime that could be built ahead of
  time.** **[review]**
- **A spec needs an implementer and a date, or it isn't written.** **[review]**
- **Only implemented specs bind.** A document with no running code behind it is a
  proposal, and a proposal cannot block a PR or justify a check. **[review]**

## Agents

- **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none.** An agent PR that adds a check, script,
  registry, config file, or design doc needs explicit human approval saying so. **[review]**
- **2026-09-06 session exception:** the user delegated the search implementation
  decisions; one `snapback2-core/build.rs` may generate pinned Unicode tables at
  build time, alongside the existing package build. No new gate, registry,
  runtime generator, or Unicode dependency is authorized by this exception. **[review]**
- **Snapback 2 LLPs are numbered 1000 and up**; `llp-create` must be told. **[review]**
- **Snapback 4 LLPs are numbered 3000 and up** (`snapback4/`, LLP 3000); it adopts these budgets
  and loop shape as its own and keeps its scope in `snapback4/NOT-DOING.md`. **[review]**

## Shared machines

- Warm, named lanes, one per stream of work. Never clone fresh; reuse the worktree.
- **Never `git stash`.** Use a temporary commit.
- Kill only PIDs you recorded at launch. Never by name or pattern.

snapback4/NOT-DOING.md
# What Snapback 4 Does Not Do

Longer than the doing-list on purpose. Moving something off it means writing one
line naming what it unblocks and taking something off the doing-list in the same
change. Nothing comes off during slice one (LLP 3000 §3: the clock is four weeks).

## The bars

The bakeoff gates in [LLP 3000 §3](../llp/3000-snapback4.explainer.md) are the
bars: the loop bar, hub acquisition within 2× the measured floor, client bytes
under the competitor-anchored budgets, the six scenarios green in the simulator
on the hub fixture. Everything not required to pass them does not exist yet.

## Not building

- **A second authoring language.** Quarry, one spelling, copied from Snapback 2 (LLP 1004, LLP 1007 §4b). TypeScript is for seeds, journeys, effect bodies and the client.
- **Byte- and step-priced certification.** No closure, heap, output or step ceilings at `check`; the certificate certifies shape, uniformity, completeness class and prediction eligibility. Resources are metered at runtime (LLP 2000.000 §6).
- **A per-query result cache.** No range receipts, validators, halos, absence evidence, coverage spans, extent facts, held directories, fact integrity or swap journals. The client replicates declared partitions with one watermark each (LLP 2000.000 §7).
- **Engine-minted ids for client inserts, grants, ID slices.** Ids are client-minted, time-ordered, 128-bit; the engine mints for its own writes.
- **The `drain` protocol, follower-tab inbox rows, `defineItems`, `withHistory`, `mutationTarget`, `receipt.source`, `local.caughtUp`, `partial` reason codes.** The card (`packages/snapback4/src/contract.ts`) is the whole client vocabulary; `why` carries the rest.
- **`retain` as a receipt rule.** `until-revoked` and `delivered-history` survive as the client's leave policy on a scope tombstone.
- **JavaScript in the data plane.** Queries and mutations run in the Rust interpreter inside the SQLite transaction, and in the same interpreter on the client (host decided at week 3 by measurement, LLP 2000.000 §9). A *job* may be the app's own Rust, hosted as wasm through the interpreter's operations under the job's meter (LLP 3000.005, the Moves line below); a query or mutation may not.
- **An embedded JS engine for effects.** The data plane never calls out. `emit` writes the effect durably in the mutation's commit and an external worker holding a service token claims, performs and settles it over the wire (`snapback4/worker`); the four reference effects run on the builder's Node (LLP 2000.000 §10, decided 2026-09-13).
- **Committed generated code; an auth mode; a supervised bundler.** As Snapback 2 (`rules/NOT-DOING.md`): types by inference, personas not modes, `SNAPBACK_URL` is the client contract.
- **A TypeScript twin of the interpreter.** Retired by the author's ruling of 2026-09-13 (LLP 3000 §7): one implementation, in Rust, on every host — the core's SQLite under the native module, memory under wasm on the web with the host persisting each commit's changes. The web pays 312,924 B gzip before the diet where the twin's tier paid 16,842; the conformance obligation between two interpreters ends. Expo Go runs the online tier.
- **More than one hosted target, an admin console, media transcoding or thumbnails, push delivery itself (a worker's), cron syntax beyond `every N at HH:MM`, vector or relevance-ranked search (word-prefix search is in: `words(..)` and `matching`), federation, multi-region, device-to-device sync, at-rest encryption claims.** After the clock, on evidence.
- **General observability beyond `why`, `trace`, `logs`, `data`, `sql`, server operation latency, and bounded client subscription inspection.** The `sql` verb is read-only inspection of the developer's own store (LLP 3000.007 §8.8), never an application surface. Separately declared application SQL reads are admitted for increment D (LLP 3000.009 §6.2, §14.4; the 2026-09-16 Moves line below), not implemented by this inspection verb.
- **A guide corpus.** The compiler's facts, one language card and keyword cards, as Snapback 2; no freshness dates. Every card's Quarry is compiled by the suite and the language card is run, so a card cannot promise a form the parser refuses.

- **Partial union delivery, two group audiences, a public branch.** A union syncs principal-column branches and at most one group branch, each a whole disjunct of the read rule (LLP 3000.036.000.000); a branch with an extra condition, a second group or a `public` branch is refused with the rewrite, never partially delivered; service grants add no device audience (LLP 3000.007 §20.6). A union does not combine with delivered history, read-through children, synced or row-keyed views, owner keys, timelines, private field owners, acquisition windows or direct/inherited expiry on content or membership scopes.
- **Exact horizon maintenance.** The horizon bounds acquisition (a snapshot, a bootstrap); the log never evicts or back-fills to hold a device's group at exactly N rows. A local read past the acquired horizon by key says `complete: false`.

- **Clock expressions in rules.** A read rule compares with `=` and `!=` only; `.expiresAt > now` remains a mutation `require`. Stored lifetimes use `not before .col` for server-controlled opening and `expire at .col` for expiry. The engine publishes opening commits; devices receive no unopened payload. The supported compositions and explicit exclusions are in LLP 3000.036.003.
- **A jobs framework.** No priorities, worker pools or dead letters: one FIFO of runs, one chunk at a time, a refused chunk parked with its refusal. Actions, effects and scheduled actions carry per-operation retries, deadlines and cancellation, and a record per external step (LLP 3000.009 §5.2; the Moves line below). Missed period boundaries while a server is down fire once on return, not once per missed period.
- **Asset processing.** No transcoding, thumbnails, rungs or HEIC: the bytes are served as uploaded; JPEG, PNG, WebP and MP4 only; image dimensions and optional MP4 duration read from the header; MP4 dimensions are not extracted.
- **Search beyond word prefixes.** One tokenizer (NFC, lowercase, alphanumeric words), one index shape (`scope, words(cols), order.., id`), one read (`matching`): every term a prefix of some word, the first term's words merged as lanes, bounded by the meter in a uniform scope, at most 32 words in an admitted non-uniform scope. No stemming, no ranking by relevance, no phrase or mid-word matching, no per-language folding, no intersection index for the second term (it filters the page).
- **An identity provider.** Guests, password accounts, service seats, and sessions a service mints for accounts the application authenticated itself. No phone, OAuth, magic links or MFA in the engine: an application's worker verifies those and mints the session.
- **No multi-server presence, no presence history or last-seen storage, no broadcast event stream, no connection-bound rows.** `connected[p]` stays server-wide, counting held polls and their 35 s grace; a live query that may read it re-runs in the background about every 5 seconds to stay current (LLP 3000.018). Typing and viewing use short-lived, authorized ephemeral tables in one server process (LLP 3000.017); they never sync or decide durable invariants. A device does not know presence and says so.

## Process not doing

- **2026-09-28 — ordinary mixed search** (LLP 3000.028 §3.3, lane OS round 1).
  Admit the SDK's bounded merge of current server rows and certified Left images
  for the proved single time-ordered word page. This removes application-owned
  online/held selection for that shape. One server call per requested page;
  recomputation pays again from consumed positions. The coordinator shares the
  existing device read allowance. No durable search session, extra synced rows,
  new authority or additional allowance is admitted.

- **2026-09-28 — inferred current-scope word search** (LLP 3000.028 §3.3,
  lane OS). A single bare ordinary word page may derive the exact non-expiring
  membership audience for the existing compact server plan. This removes the
  requirement to repeat that audience predicate in this narrow server query.
  The compiler supplies a scoped words index when absent; it is an ordinary
  schema index, maintained on writes and on devices, with no extra synced rows
  or new authority. The device keeps its original bare scan. Round 0 left ordered composition
  and combined accounting outside its independent subset; round 1 above admits
  that bounded SDK composition. Durable search sessions remain excluded.
- **2026-10-12 — union sync audiences** (LLP 3000.036.000.000, workstream UNION, two blind review rounds). A table syncs to the union of principal-column audiences and one group audience; a device holds a row while any branch admits its viewer. What it unblocks: owner-or-team, buyer-or-seller and owner-or-staff tables offline for every reader, the shape three app farms asked for. Taken off: "one `sync` audience per table". Partial delivery, two groups and a public branch stay excluded (above).
- **2026-09-28 — explicit owner-key coverage** (LLP 3000.028 §3.4, Lane OK commission). A public window may opt into a compiler-owned, horizon-free principal key partition to answer ordinary own-key existence offline. Taken off: the exclusion of narrower platform key distribution beside one public window. General union audiences, full own-row replication and per-query absence caches remain excluded. The projection uses existing metered maintains, adoption and whole-partition publication; existing windows do not expand.
- **2026-09-26 — a live query keeps presence current** (LLP 3000.018). A 0.4.2 probe found an observed `connected[p]` reporting `fresh: true` while stale for over a minute, and a comparative builder polled around it. What it unblocks: online marks and presence-aware lists that stay current. Taken off: "a presence stream" as an exclusion for live queries; a presence API, last-seen storage and multi-server presence stay out. Under the author's standing authorization for reworks that make queries excellent (2026-09-25).

- **No drift registries, inventories, line-pinned diagnostics registries, claim digests or frozen-record gates.** Generated projections are built, not committed.
- **No gate bound to an exact commit; no push gated on a battery.** Five blocking checks in sixty seconds, run before push; everything slower on a schedule with bounded tickets.
- **No ceiling raised in slice one.** Budgets are anchored to a competitor's measured number and recorded once in the journal.
- **No standing panel** except the two blind reviews LLP 3000 decision 4 names (partition inversion; the meter's cut on non-uniform scans). The author explicitly commissioned the one-off LLP 3000.008 panel and disjoint Astra implementation lanes on 2026-09-14; its bounded disposition is recorded in that umbrella and LLP 3000 §7.
- **No new LLP number** without first extending LLP 3000 or LLP 2000.000; no spec without running code (`rules/RULES.md`: only implemented specs bind).
- **No second session on the core** during slice one; lanes take the periphery.
- **No test matrix as the primary harness.** The simulator is; real-browser and device witnesses cover only what it cannot reach.
- **No files over 1,500 lines**, including ones copied from Snapback 2. Split on
  the way in. The one exception is the package's published documents
  (`packages/snapback4/README.md` and its linked references): the rule exists to
  keep a *source* file reviewable, and the 0.2.25 calibration measured the cost of
  applying it to a document — splitting the README was that run's single largest
  scoring loss, because the builder then had four places to look instead of one
  (LLP 3000.007 §20.19). A published document is bounded by whether a builder can
  find one way in, not by a line count; the census that enforces this rule covers
  source, and says so.

## Deliberately worse

- No compatibility with Snapback 1 or Snapback 2 apps, packages or on-disk formats.
- No API stability before the clock; every publish is `0.0.x`.
- Sparse prose documentation; the diagnostics and the recipes carry the load.
- One hosted target, one platform binary at a time. SQLite remains the default store; Postgres deploy/serve admits the initial Unix-socket HTTP profile under LLP 3000.009.001 (Moves, 2026-10-20; `guide release-json`). Provider HA, full parity and publication remain outside that profile.

## Moves

- **2026-10-20 — Snapback 4 on Postgres moves onto the doing-list** (author: "commit and push these things, then do your \"what i'd do next\" things, then get this working on postgres and measure it"; LLP 3000.009.001 and its children). Unblocks: the store-port extraction on SQLite (P0, including the `Committer` seam with the serial batch); the Postgres adapters for every durable-state family and `serve`/`deploy`/`doctor` over Postgres (P1), with store-held fencing, the declared HA mode and `BlobStore`; the optimistic committer, commissioned on 2026-10-19 and built after its execution stage is sized; the scale program of LLP 3000.009.001.002 with its raw-Postgres, Supabase and Convex controls on fleet machines; and a research note comparing replicated SQLite with Postgres for applications that outgrow one SQLite file. Per-application jobs that flip a publication flag leave this admitted path; clock expressions in rules, captured lower lifetimes for read-through children, and boundary recounts for maintained data remain excluded. /** @throws None at construction; locator observation can refuse ambiguous or invalid selectors. */
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — composed text preserves exactness and ambiguity.
export function renderedText(page: Page, text: string | RegExp, options: { within?: Locator; exact?: boolean } | null = {}): Locator {
  const normalized = options ?? {};
  const root = normalized.within ?? page;
  const match = (exact: boolean) => registeredLocator(root.locator(`${renderedSelector}=${JSON.stringify({
    source: typeof text === "string" ? text : text.source,
    flags: typeof text === "string" ? "" : text.flags,
    regex: typeof text !== "string", exact,
  })}`));
  const locator = match(normalized.exact ?? true);
  if (typeof text === "string" && normalized.exact !== false) substringLocators.set(locator, { locator: match(false), scoped: normalized.within !== undefined });
  return locator;
}

export interface ExhaustPagesOptions {
  /** Refuse rather than loop forever when a backend returns bad continuations. */
  maxPages?: number;
  /** Names the read in a refusal without exposing its rows or cursor. */
  label?: string;
}
type ProofPage<Row> =
  | { readonly data: readonly Row[]; readonly next?: Cursor | null; readonly complete: boolean; readonly cut: ReadCut; readonly existence?: "present" | "absent" | "partial" }
  | { readonly denied: Refusal }
  | { readonly loading: true };
/** Read every page by passing each opaque `next` back unchanged. The callback
 * receives null first. Refusals, loading, malformed/repeated cursors and a
 * capped or incomplete page fail instead of returning a partial snapshot. */
/** @throws E_PROOF_PAGE for a refused, loading, malformed, repeated, incomplete or over-limit traversal; callback errors propagate. */
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — proof traversal must never promote capped or partial reads to complete evidence.
export async function exhaustPages<Row>(readPage: (cursor: Cursor | null) => Promise<ProofPage<Row>>, options: ExhaustPagesOptions = {}): Promise<Row[]> {
  const maxPages = options.maxPages ?? 1_000, label = options.label ?? "paged read";
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(maxPages) || maxPages < 1) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: maxPages must be a positive safe integer`);
  const rows: Row[] = [], seen = new Set<string>();
  let cursor: Cursor | null = null;
  for (let pageNumber = 1; pageNumber <= maxPages; pageNumber++) {
    const page = await readPage(cursor);
    if (!page || typeof page !== "object") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned no read envelope`);
    if ("denied" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} refused ${page.denied.code}: ${page.denied.message}`);
    if ("loading" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is still loading`);
    if (!Array.isArray(page.data)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} data is not an array`);
    if (page.cut !== null) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (${page.cut === undefined ? "missing" : page.cut} cut)`);
    if (page.complete !== true) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (complete must be true)`);
    if (page.existence === "partial") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} has partial existence`);
    rows.push(...page.data);
    const next = page.next ?? null;
    if (next === null) return rows;
    if (typeof next !== "string" || next.length === 0) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a malformed cursor`);
    if (seen.has(next)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a repeated cursor`);
    seen.add(next);
    cursor = next as Cursor;
  }
  throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: exceeded maxPages ${maxPages}`);
}

#[test]
fn dx8_each_preserves_optional_null_and_narrows_removed_old_list_elements() {
    let optional = OLD_EACH.replace("names: [file <=1000] <=8", "names: [file <=1000] <=8 ?");
    let mut e = engine(&optional);
    let parent = mutate(&mut e, "add", [("names", Value::Null)])
        .field("id")
        .unwrap()
        .as_str()
        .unwrap()
        .to_owned();
    adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
    adopt(&mut e, &optional, 1).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(field(&mut e, "orders", &parent, "names"), Value::Null);
    let mut e = engine(OLD_EACH);
    let a = handle(&mut e, b"a");
    let b = handle(&mut e, b"b");
    let parent = mutate(&mut e, "add", [("names", Value::Array(vec![a, b]))])
        .field("id")
        .unwrap()
        .as_str()
        .unwrap()
        .to_owned();
    adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
    adopt(&mut e, OLD_EACH, 1).unwrap();
    let Value::Array(mut values) = field(&mut e, "orders", &parent, "names") else {
        panic!()
    };
    let removed = values.pop().unwrap();
    let removed_id = crate::assets::asset_id(Some(&removed)).unwrap().to_owned();
    mutate(
        &mut e,
        "edit",
        [("id", Value::Id(parent)), ("names", Value::Array(values))],
    );
    adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        e.store().count("documents").unwrap(),
        1,
        "removed element cannot regain an active asset home"
    );
    for _ in 0..3 {
        adopt(&mut e, OLD_EACH, 1).unwrap();
        adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e.store().count("documents").unwrap(), 1);
        let released = e.store().asset(&removed_id).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(released.home.is_none(), "removed asset must have no active home after repeated migration cycles");
        assert!(released.released_at.is_some(), "removed asset remains eligible for ordinary garbage collection");
    }
}
#[test]
fn dx8_each_refuses_to_rebind_a_native_child_to_a_reused_parent_lifetime() {
    let mut e = engine(NEW_EACH);
    let a = handle(&mut e, b"a");
    let aid = crate::assets::asset_id(Some(&a)).unwrap().to_owned();
    mutate(
        &mut e,
        "attach",
        [("order", Value::Id("missing-parent".into())), ("names", a)],
    );
    seed(&mut e, "orders", json!({"id":"missing-parent"}));
    let generation = e.generation();
    let error = adopt(&mut e, OLD_EACH, 1).unwrap_err().to_string();
    assert!(error.contains("parent-lifetime evidence"), "{error}");
    assert_eq!(e.generation(), generation);
    assert_eq!(
        e.store().asset(&aid).unwrap().unwrap().home.unwrap().0,
        "documents"
    );
}

fn dx8_each_requires_immutable_captured_parent_audience_before_activation() {
    let next = NEW_EACH
        .replacen(
            "  public 'fixture'",
            "  owner: principal\n  read <- .owner = viewer\n  update <- allow",
            1,
        )
        .replacen(
            "  public 'fixture'",
            "  immutable order\n  read through .order",
            1,
        );
    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("unsafe.q".into(), next)]);
    assert!(
        bound
            .diagnostics
            .iter()
            .any(|d| d.code == "E_READ_THROUGH" && d.message.contains("must be immutable")),
        "{:?}",
        bound.diagnostics
    );
}

#[test]
fn dx8_each_restores_suspended_children_without_replaying_consumed_lists() {
    let suspended=NEW_EACH.split("\ntable documents:").next().unwrap().to_owned()+"\nmutation add():\n  return insert orders {}\n";
    let mut e=engine(OLD_EACH);
    let a=handle(&mut e,b"original");
    let parent=mutate(&mut e,"add",[("names",Value::Array(vec![a]))]).field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
    adopt(&mut e,NEW_EACH,2).unwrap();
    let image=handle(&mut e,b"edited current");let aid=crate::assets::asset_id(Some(&image)).unwrap().to_owned();
    let child=e.store().test_support_conn().query_row("SELECT id FROM r WHERE t=(SELECT num FROM _catalog WHERE name='documents')",[],|r|r.get::<_,String>(0)).unwrap();
    mutate(&mut e,"edit",[("id",Value::Id(child.clone())),("names",image)]);
    let native=handle(&mut e,b"native current");let bid=crate::assets::asset_id(Some(&native)).unwrap().to_owned();
    let native=mutate(&mut e,"attach",[("order",Value::Id(parent.clone())),("names",native)]).field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
    for cycle in 0..3 {
        adopt(&mut e,&suspended,3).unwrap();
        if cycle==0 {mutate(&mut e,"add",[]);}
        adopt(&mut e,NEW_EACH,2).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e.store().count("documents").unwrap(),2);
        assert_eq!(child_for(&e,&aid),child);assert_eq!(child_for(&e,&bid),native);
        assert!(e.store().adoption_report().backfills.iter().any(|x|x.contains("without replaying consumed")));
    }
    adopt(&mut e,OLD_EACH,1).unwrap();assert_eq!(ids(&mut e,&parent),vec![aid,bid]);

//! SQLite erases booleans to integers. Recover direct column types from the
//! adopted schema and SQL projection, never by guessing from names or 0/1.
// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.26 — positional JSON stays compatible; boolean recovery is presentation on the operator's adopted snapshot.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — direct schema-proven media cells use their ordinary wire JSON in object rows.
use snapback4_core::{inspection::InspectionColumnKind as Kind, schema::{ColumnType, Schema}};
use sqlparser::{ast::{Expr, ObjectName, Query, SelectItem, SelectItemQualifiedWildcardKind, SetExpr, Statement, TableFactor}, dialect::SQLiteDialect, parser::Parser};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

type Columns = Vec<(String, Kind)>;
type Tables = BTreeMap<String, Columns>;

pub(super) fn kinds(sql: &str, schema: &Schema, count: usize, retained: bool) -> Result<Vec<Kind>, String> {
    let mut tables: Tables = schema.visible_tables().map(|(name, table)| {
        let mut columns = vec![("id".into(), Kind::Plain)];
        columns.extend(table.columns.iter().filter(|(name, _)| *name != "id")
            .map(|(name, kind)| (name.to_ascii_lowercase(), if matches!(kind.required(), ColumnType::Bool) { Kind::Bool } else if kind.contains_asset() { Kind::Media } else { Kind::Plain })));
        if retained {columns.extend([("_snapback_state".into(),Kind::Plain),("_snapback_source".into(),Kind::Plain),("_snapback_columns".into(),Kind::Plain)]);}
        (name.to_ascii_lowercase(), columns)
    }).collect();
    let statements = Parser::parse_sql(&SQLiteDialect {}, sql).map_err(|e| format!("--json-objects SQL projection: {e}; use --json for SQLite-specific syntax"))?;
    let [Statement::Query(query)] = statements.as_slice() else { return Err("--json-objects takes a SELECT".into()); };
    let columns = query_columns(query, &mut tables)?;
    if columns.len() != count { return Err("--json-objects cannot determine this projection's column types; select explicit columns or use --json".into()); }
    Ok(columns.into_iter().map(|(_, kind)| kind).collect())
}

fn name(name: &ObjectName) -> Option<String> {
    // SQLite schema qualification bypasses CTE shadowing; do not erase it.
    if name.0.len() != 1 { return None; }
    name.0.last()?.as_ident().map(|id| id.value.to_ascii_lowercase())
}

fn query_columns(query: &Query, inherited: &mut Tables) -> Result<Columns, String> {
    let mut tables = inherited.clone();
    if let Some(with) = &query.with {
        if with.recursive { return Err("--json-objects does not infer recursive CTE types; use --json".into()); }
        for cte in &with.cte_tables {
            if tables.contains_key(&cte.alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()) {
                return Err("--json-objects does not infer shadowing CTEs; use --json".into());
            }
            let mut columns = query_columns(&cte.query, &mut tables)?;
            for (column, alias) in columns.iter_mut().zip(&cte.alias.columns) { column.0 = alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase(); }
            tables.insert(cte.alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase(), columns);
        }
    }
    set_columns(&query.body, &mut tables)
}

fn relation(factor: &TableFactor, tables: &mut Tables) -> Result<(String, Columns), String> {
    match factor {
        TableFactor::Table { name: object, alias, args: None, .. } => {
            let key = name(object).ok_or("--json-objects does not infer schema-qualified relations; use --json")?;
            let columns = tables.get(&key).ok_or("--json-objects needs application tables or typed CTEs")?.clone();
            Ok((alias.as_ref().map(|a| a.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()).unwrap_or(key), columns))
        }
        TableFactor::Derived { subquery, alias, .. } => Ok((alias.as_ref().map(|a| a.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()).unwrap_or_default(), query_columns(subquery, tables)?)),
        _ => Err("--json-objects cannot infer this table expression; use --json".into()),
    }
}

fn set_columns(body: &SetExpr, tables: &mut Tables) -> Result<Columns, String> {
    match body {
        SetExpr::Query(q) => query_columns(q, tables),
        SetExpr::SetOperation { left, right, .. } => {
            let mut left = set_columns(left, tables)?;
            let right = set_columns(right, tables)?;
            if left.len() != right.len() { return Err("incompatible SQL projections".into()); }
            for (l, r) in left.iter_mut().zip(right) { if l.1 != r.1 { l.1 = Kind::Plain; } }
            Ok(left)
        }
        SetExpr::Select(select) => {
            let mut sources = Vec::new();
            for from in &select.from {
                sources.push(relation(&from.relation, tables)?);
                for join in &from.joins { sources.push(relation(&join.relation, tables)?); }
            }
            let mut output = Vec::new();
            for item in &select.projection {
                match item {
                    SelectItem::Wildcard(_) => output.extend(sources.iter().flat_map(|(_, cols)| cols.clone())),
                    SelectItem::QualifiedWildcard(SelectItemQualifiedWildcardKind::ObjectName(object), _) => {
                        let key = name(object).ok_or("unsupported wildcard")?;
                        let (_, cols) = sources.iter().find(|(alias, _)| *alias == key).ok_or("unknown wildcard table")?;
                        output.extend(cols.clone());
                    }
                    SelectItem::UnnamedExpr(expr) => {
                        let mut direct = expr;
                        while let Expr::Nested(inner) = direct { direct = inner; }
                        let label = match direct {
                            Expr::Identifier(id) => id.value.clone(),
                            Expr::CompoundIdentifier(ids) => ids.last().unwrap().value.clone(),
                            _ => expr.to_string(),
                        };
                        output.push((label.to_ascii_lowercase(), kind(expr, &sources)));
                    }
                    SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr, alias } => output.push((alias.value.to_ascii_lowercase(), kind(expr, &sources))),
                    _ => return Err("unsupported object-row projection; use --json".into()),
                }
            }
            let mut names = BTreeSet::new();
            if output.iter().any(|(name, _)| !names.insert(name)) {
                return Err("--json-objects needs unique names in every projection; alias duplicate columns".into());
            }
            Ok(output)
        }
        _ => Err("--json-objects needs a SELECT projection; use --json".into()),
    }
}

fn kind(expr: &Expr, sources: &[(String, Columns)]) -> Kind {
    let (table, column) = match expr {
        Expr::Nested(expr) => return kind(expr, sources),
        Expr::Identifier(id) => (None, &id.value),
        Expr::CompoundIdentifier(ids) if ids.len() == 2 => (Some(ids[0].value.to_ascii_lowercase()), &ids[1].value),
        _ => return Kind::Plain, // Computed SQL expressions retain SQLite's own types.
    };
    let found: Vec<Kind> = sources.iter().filter(|(alias, _)| table.as_ref().is_none_or(|t| t == alias))
        .flat_map(|(_, cols)| cols.iter().filter(|(name, _)| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(column)).map(|(_, kind)| *kind)).collect();
    // An unqualified duplicate only reaches execution when SQLite resolved it
    // through USING/NATURAL. All contributors must agree before typing it bool.
    found.first().copied().filter(|first| found.iter().all(|kind| kind == first)).unwrap_or(Kind::Plain)
}

//! Referential actions on delete (LLP 3000.039 §3): before a delete removes
//! its row, reserve a schema-fixed charge, close over the `cascade`
//! references, refuse while a `restrict` reference still holds a closure row
//! from outside the closure, clear `set null` references outside it, and
//! remove the closure children first. The caller then removes the row itself.
// @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — closure first; probes exclude the closure; deletion dominates set null.
use crate::engine::runner::Runner;
use crate::{
    error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError},
    meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter},
    rows::{Bounds, Dir},
    schema::{Effect, references::{OnDelete, Referencing}},
    value::Value,
};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

impl Runner<'_> {
    pub(super) fn apply_reference_actions(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.reference_actions(table_name, old, false)
    }

    // Recovery has no later root-delete hook to preflight physical read-through
    // retention. Include that root before the first child action can write.
    pub(in crate::engine) fn apply_missing_reference_actions(&mut self, table_name: &str, identity: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.reference_actions(table_name, identity, true)
    }

    fn reference_actions(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value, missing_root: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        if !schema.is_referenced(table_name) { return Ok(()); }
        let Some(price) = schema.delete_reservation(table_name) else {
            // A device without a reached child's exported price cannot charge
            // what the server charges; the server always has every price.
            if self.device { return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting {table_name} needs every referencing table's write price; queued without a local delete"))); }
            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table_name}'s delete actions have no reservation: a cascading reference lacks its cap or its child's write price (guide writes)")));
        };
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#4.2 — what the commit publishes is fixed by the schema, not by the rows the actions reach.
        let closure = schema.action_tables(table_name);
        // A public device projection carries the private column's price but
        // not the maintain that computes its value. If an action can write
        // such a source, settlement must supply the authoritative mirror.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007.001#3.7 — devices store maintained columns but never derive them.
        if self.device && closure.written.iter().any(|source| schema.write_reservation(source)
            .is_some_and(|plan| plan.price(crate::schema::reservations::COLUMNS)[3] != 0)) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting {table_name} can change a server-maintained column; queued without a local delete")));
        }
        for table in &closure.written {
            if schema.visible(table) { self.written_tables.insert(table.clone()); }
            self.action_tables.insert(table.clone());
        }
        for table in &closure.read { self.read_tables.insert(table.clone()); }
        if !closure.written.is_empty() { self.tx.widen_change_evidence(); }
        for (kind, amount) in [(MeterKind::Steps, price[0]), (MeterKind::IndexEntries, price[1]), (MeterKind::Examined, price[2]), (MeterKind::RowsWritten, price[3]), (MeterKind::OutputBytes, price[5]), (MeterKind::RuleProbes, price[6])] {
            if amount > 0 { self.meter.charge(kind, amount)?; }
        }
        // Pending event images survive the closure and subsequent statements.
        // Keep their schema-fixed reservation until the request ends.
        let events = schema.delete_event_heap(table_name).unwrap_or(0);
        self.meter.heap(events)?;
        let mark = self.meter.mark();
        self.meter.heap(price[4].saturating_sub(events))?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — draw the reservation's rows from the request's physical allowance before the first seek.
        if !self.context.is_system() { self.tx.draw(table_name, price[2])?; }
        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort));
        // The fixed action reservation prepays the closure itself, but held-
        // group and authority proofs remain device-only bounded work. Keep the
        // active allowance reachable by nested `device_work` calls while the
        // closure runs under its prepaid unbounded meter. Recursive cascade
        // removals see the already-stored allowance and must not take it over.
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — every device-only proof spends the separate bounded physical-work allowance.
        let owns_device_allowance = self.device_work_active && self.device_allowance.is_none();
        let mut meter = Some(meter);
        if owns_device_allowance { self.device_allowance = meter.take(); }
        let prepaid = self.tx.reference_prepaid(true);
        let action = std::mem::replace(&mut self.engine_action, true);
        let result = self.reference_closure(table_name, old, missing_root);
        self.engine_action = action;
        self.tx.reference_prepaid(prepaid);
        self.meter = if owns_device_allowance {
            self.device_allowance.take().expect("active device allowance")
        } else {
            meter.expect("prepaid action meter")
        };
        self.meter.release_heap(mark);
        result
    }

    /// Steps 3–6. The walk holds identities, never images: each child scan
    /// streams `PAGE` rows per seek, and every write rereads its row current.
    fn reference_closure(&mut self, root_table: &str, root: &Value, missing_root: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        let mut seen: BTreeSet<(String, String)> = BTreeSet::from([(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned())]);
        // (Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.)
        let mut visits: Vec<(String, Value)> = vec![(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.clone())];
        // 3. Close over cascades, breadth first. Every reached row's referencing groups must be held on a device.
        let mut next = 0;
        while next < visits.len() {
            let (table, id) = visits[next].clone();
            next += 1;
            for r in schema.referencing(&table) {
                if self.device && !through_reference(&r) { self.prove_reference_held(&r, &id)?; }
                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }
                self.each_child(&r, &id, true, &mut |_, child| {
                    if seen.insert((r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned())) { visits.push((r.child.to_owned(), child)); }
                    Ok(true)
                })?;
            }
        }
        // 4. Restrict: every probe runs, streaming past closure rows (the root
        // included) to the first outside witness; the first occupied reference
        // in schema order is reported. One reference's probes visit each closure
        // row at most once, plus one witness per probe (LLP 3000.039 §5.1).
        let mut occupied: Option<(String, String, String)> = None;
        for (table, id) in &visits {
            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
                if r.action != OnDelete::Restrict || through_reference(&r) { continue; }
                let mut outside = false;
                self.each_child(&r, id, false, &mut |_, child| {
                    outside = !seen.contains(&(r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned()));
                    Ok(!outside)
                })?;
                let candidate = (r.child.to_owned(), r.column.to_owned(), table.clone());
                if outside && occupied.as_ref().is_none_or(|o| candidate < *o) { occupied = Some(candidate); }
            }
        }
        if let Some((child, column, parent)) = occupied {
            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
            self.refusing_clause(&child, &format!("{column}: {parent} (on delete restrict)"));
            let via = if parent == root_table { String::new() } else { format!(", through a {parent} row this delete cascades to") };
            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED", message: format!("{root_table} at {} is still referenced through {child}.{column} (on delete restrict){via}; delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)", self.statement_site) });
        }
        // A cascaded row can itself have a physically retained read-through
        // child. Decide that blocker before set-null writes begin, so expiry
        // can retain this root and continue without relying on transaction
        // rollback to undo a partial closure.
        for (table, id) in visits.iter().skip(if missing_root { 0 } else { 1 }) {
            if self.physical_children_outside(table, id, &seen)? {
                return Err(self.parent_has_children(table));
            }
        }
        // 5. Set null outside the closure. Each group is gathered whole before
        // any of it is cleared: a clear can recount a sibling that shares the
        // reference's index and move it behind a page cursor. Each row is then
        // reread current before its write.
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — gather, then clear: no row moves out of a walk it has not finished.
        for (table, id) in &visits {
            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
                if r.action != OnDelete::SetNull { continue; }
                let mut group: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
                self.each_child(&r, id, true, &mut |_, child| {
                    let child = child.as_str()?.to_owned();
                    if !seen.contains(&(r.child.to_owned(), child.clone())) { group.push(child); }
                    Ok(true)
                })?;
                for child in group {
                    let current = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, r.child, &child))?;
                    if let Some(current) = current.filter(|row| row.field(r.column).is_ok_and(|v| v == id)) {
                        self.clear_reference(r.child, r.column, current)?;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // 6. Delete the closure, children first, each from its current image.
        let reached: Vec<(String, String)> = visits[1..].iter().map(|(t, id)| Ok((t.clone(), id.as_str()?.to_owned()))).collect::<Result<_, RuntimeError>>()?;
        drop(visits);
        for (table, id) in deletion_order(schema, &reached) {
            let current = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &table, &id))?;
            let Some(current) = current else { continue };
            self.delete_reached(&table, current)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Streams the ids of the live rows referencing `id` through `r` to
    /// `visit`, through its index, until `visit` answers false. A capped walk
    /// (cascade, set null) reads `PAGE` rows per seek and holds at most the
    /// reference's cap; a restrict probe reads one row per seek, so it examines
    /// nothing past its witness. Images are dropped before `visit` runs. Seeks
    /// start at the live suffix, so an expired backlog is never visited.
    fn each_child(&mut self, r: &Referencing<'_>, id: &Value, capped: bool, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Self, Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        let index = schema.reference_index(r.child, r.column).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} has no reference index", r.child, r.column)))?.to_owned();
        let (cap, page_rows) = if capped { (schema.reference_cap(r.child, r.column).map_or(u64::MAX, u64::from), PAGE) } else { (u64::MAX, 1) };
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#2.3 — seek on the effective deadline (a read-through child's `$deadline`), so no expired row is visited.
        let ranges = if r.table.expiry_column().is_some() && !through_reference(r) {
            let now = self.context.now.ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("delete clock is not pinned".into()))?;
            vec![(vec![id.clone(), Value::Null], None), (vec![id.clone()], Some(Value::Int(now)))]
        } else {
            vec![(vec![id.clone()], None)]
        };
        let mut live = 0_u64;
        for (prefix, gt) in ranges {
            let mut bounds = Bounds { gt, ..Default::default() };
            loop {
                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, r.child, &index, &prefix, &bounds, Dir::Asc, page_rows))?;
                let more = page.len() == page_rows;
                if let Some((_, key)) = page.last() { bounds.after = crate::key::decode(key).map(|v| v.into_iter().skip(prefix.len()).collect()); }
                let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(page.len());
                for (row, _) in page {
                    if self.device {
                        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — a device predicts only over current rows: retained history queues the delete, and only a live, current (or own provisional) row is a witness.
                        // A retained, no longer current row is work the reservation does not
                        // price and a witness the device cannot judge: the delete queues.
                        if self.tx.retained_row(r.child, &row)? && !self.tx.current_row(r.child, &row)? {
                            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting meets retained {} history that references it; queued without a local delete", r.child)));
                        }
                        if self.expired(r.table, &row) || !(self.tx.current_row(r.child, &row)? || self.is_provisional(r.child, &row)?) {
                            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting needs a current image of every {} row that references it; queued without a local delete", r.child)));
                        }
                    } else if self.expired(r.table, &row) { continue; }
                    live += 1;
                    // Activation validates caps and every write keeps them; more than the cap
                    // is a store that broke its own invariant, never a hidden-row count.
                    if live > cap { return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} holds more rows than its cap for one {} row", r.child, r.column, r.column))); }
                    ids.push(row.field("id")?.clone());
                }
                for child in ids {
                    if !visit(self, child)? { return Ok(()); }
                }
                if !more { break; }

//! Release row lifetimes whose present values cannot inhabit the selected type.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#91-per-row-narrowed-value-dormancy — hide a reference-closed population; never coerce values.
use super::*;
use crate::schema::{ColumnType, Constraint};

pub(super) fn present(conn: &Connection) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    Ok(conn.query_row(
        "SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name='_dormant_narrow_rows')",
        [],
        |r| r.get(0),
    )?)

fn incompatible(tx:&Tx<'_>,schema: &Schema, name: &str, row: &Value) -> Result<bool,RuntimeError> {
    incompatible_except(tx,schema,name,row,&[])
}
fn incompatible_except(tx:&Tx<'_>,schema: &Schema,name:&str,row:&Value,authority:&[String])->Result<bool,RuntimeError> {
    let table = &schema.tables[name];
    for (column,kind) in &table.columns {
        if table.engine_field(column) || table.maintained.contains_key(column) || authority.contains(column) {continue;}
        if let Ok(value)=row.field(column) {
            if incompatible_column(tx, table, name, column, kind, value)? { return Ok(true); }
        }
    }
    Ok(false)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#11-wave-11-factual-release-narration — the warning and activation share the value predicate, including ledger-backed assets.
pub(super) fn incompatible_column(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: &Table, name: &str, column: &str, kind: &ColumnType, value: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    if crate::engine::validate::validate_column(name, column, kind, Some(value)).is_err() { return Ok(true); }
    // @ref LLP 3000.038#1-the-type — asset facts belong to the ledger, including optional/list leaves.
    match super::activation::validate_assets(tx, kind, Some(value)) {
        Err(RuntimeError::Asset { code: "E_ASSET_TYPE" | "E_ASSET_TOO_LARGE", .. }) => return Ok(true),
        Err(error) => return Err(error),
        Ok(()) => (),
    }
    Ok(table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::Text { field, min, format }
        if field == column && matches!(value, Value::String(s)
            if crate::engine::validate::validate_text(field, s, *min, *format).is_err()))))
}

fn migratable(kind:&ColumnType)->bool {
    match kind {ColumnType::Optional(k)=>migratable(k),ColumnType::Image{..}|ColumnType::Video{..}|ColumnType::File{..}|ColumnType::List{..}|ColumnType::ListRange{..}|ColumnType::Ref{..}=>false,_=>true}
}

fn refs(kind: &ColumnType, value: &Value, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>) {
    match (kind, value) {
        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), v) => refs(inner, v, out),
        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(vs)) => {
            for v in vs {
                refs(of, v, out);
            }
        }
        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => out.push((table.clone(), id.clone())),
        _ => {}
    }
}

    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn changed(&self, next: &Self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
        self.0.keys().chain(next.0.keys()).filter(|key| {
            let (a,b)=(self.0.get(*key),next.0.get(*key));
            if key.ends_with(".domains") {
                match (a.and_then(Value::as_object),b.and_then(Value::as_object)) {
                    (Some(a),Some(b)) => a.iter().any(|(column,kind)| b.get(column) != Some(kind)),
                    _ => a!=b,
                }
            } else {a!=b}
        })
            .map(|key| key.split('.').next().unwrap().to_owned()).collect()
    }
    pub fn changed_directional(&self, next: &Self, current: &Schema, target: &Schema) -> BTreeSet<String> {
        self.0.keys().chain(next.0.keys()).filter(|key| {
            let (a,b)=(self.0.get(*key),next.0.get(*key));
            a!=b && !key.split_once(".domain.").is_some_and(|(table,column)|domain_widens(current,target,table,column))
        }).map(|key|key.split('.').next().unwrap().to_owned()).collect()
    }

Amended proof-kit §8: **READY**. The exact adjacent-record corroboration preserves normal listener validation. Both supplied section hashes match the frozen commit.

**DX8 has one material custody gap: empty-parent re-entry skips child validation.**

At `62c38dfca5f26d01ebc67465fad25dabb734caa7`, `store/extractions.rs:346` requires `populated` before selecting `each::resume`. With zero active parents, it instead runs `each::forward`, which visits no parents and validates only existing receipts.

Concrete counterexample permitted by the frozen source:

1. Successfully initialize an empty `each` extraction.
2. Remove only its declaration, retaining the public parent/child tables.
3. Insert an independent child referencing a not-yet-existing parent P. Ordinary references permit missing targets.
4. Restore the extraction while the parent table remains empty. Adoption succeeds without checking that child’s missing extraction anchor.
5. Create P, then update the child’s asset without changing its parent reference. `extractions.rs:483–499` captures the previously missing anchor.
6. Reverse selection now accepts that child and transfers its asset into P’s historical list.

This retroactively captures a child born while the declaration was absent, contradicting the amendment’s explicit lifetime-custody guarantee.

**Required correction:** select the resume validator for known, consumed-source definitions regardless of parent population, and validate every current/restored child. Preserve legitimate empty initialization, but refuse unanchored existing children atomically. Prevent unchanged-reference updates from manufacturing missing extraction provenance. Add a regression covering this sequence and unchanged generation, format and asset homes on refusal.
